DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.claim: Qaḍā can mean doing or carrying out an act, including carrying out God’s decree and the matter of marriage.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r6.anchor: الرابع : قضى بمعنى فعل قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr use kasra on ʿayn in both occurrences of بالعدوة; the other readers use ḍamma.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r4.speaker: ابن كثير في رواية قنبل وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r4.claim: These readers assimilate the two yāʾs in حي عن بينة into one geminated yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير فى رواية قنبل وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r5.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر ونافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r5.claim: These readers pronounce two distinct yāʾs in من حيي.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r6.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r6.claim: Al-Bazzī transmits two clear yāʾs from Ibn Kathīr, as Nāfiʿ does; a further report from Shibl says the same.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ transmits one geminated yāʾ from ʿĀṣim.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r7.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم ﴿ حي ﴾ بياء واحدة مشددة

STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah centers on Badr (624 CE), the first major Muslim–Quraysh battle, fought a year after the Migration amid Quraysh's continuing hostility.
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r6.anchor: Battle of Badr (2/624), fought a year after the hijrah (the migration from Makkah to Madinah), the first major military confrontation

STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r11.claim: Badr was an important first Muslim-community victory and is cited in Qurʾānic commentary as evidence of God's favor.
STUDYQURAN:8:intro/r11.anchor: The Battle of Badr was an important first victory for the young Muslim community and is cited in the commentary on many verses in the Quran as evidence of God’s Favor upon it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p326/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p326/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقسم والحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p326/r13.claim: They identify the Quraysh chiefs killed at Badr as the leading figures meant in the account of the two armies meeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p326/r13.anchor: قتل فيها صناديد قريش نص عليه ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقسم والحسن وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r1.claim: The majority endorses the preceding account’s date for Badr; Abu Salih gives the alternative of the nineteenth of Ramadan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r1.anchor: الجمهور، وقال أبو صالح لتسعة عشر يوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r2.claim: Abu Salih gives the alternative date, the nineteenth of Ramadan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r2.anchor: وقال أبو صالح لتسعة عشر يوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r3.claim: The things sent down were the verses, angels, and victory; the passage ends by stressing divine power because God gave the smaller Muslim force victory over the larger enemy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r3.anchor: المنزل: الآيات والملائكة والنصر وختم بصفة القدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r4.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads عبدنا with two dammas; depending on the vocalization, it refers to the Messenger alone or to him together with the believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r4.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي عبدنا بضمتين كقراءة من قرأ وعبد الطاغوت بضمتين فعلى عبدنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r5.claim: يوم الفرقان is an adverb attached to وما أنزلنا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r5.anchor: وانتصاب يوم الفرقان على أنه ظرف معمول لقوله وما أنزلنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj offers a second parse: يوم modifies غنمتم, so the verse speaks of what was acquired on the day of Badr and the fifth due from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج ويحتمل أن ينتصب ب غنمتم أي أن ما غنمتم يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya calls al-Zajjaj’s sense good, but notes that the intervening clause makes the syntactic attachment difficult.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا تأويل حسن في المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r8.claim: He rejects al-Zajjaj’s syntactic parse because it separates a conditional verb from its object or a relative clause verb from its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r8.anchor: ولا يجوز ما قاله الزجاج لأنه إن كانت ما شرطية على تخريج الفراء لزم فيه الفصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r9.claim: العدوة means the bank or edge of a valley; it is named for keeping the valley’s water from passing beyond it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r9.anchor: العدوة شط الوادي وتسمي شفيرا وضفة سميت بذلك لأنها عدت ما في الوادي من ماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r10.claim: An unnamed poet’s line uses the same verb in the sense of diverting someone from a visit, illustrating the root’s meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r10.anchor: وقال الشاعر: عدتني عن زيارتها العوادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r11.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read العدوة with kasra on the ʿayn in both occurrences.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالعدوة بكسر العين فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r12.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r12.claim: The other seven canonical readers use damma on the ʿayn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r13.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وزيد بن علي وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r13.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the ʿayn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r13.anchor: والحسن وقتادة وزيد بن علي وعمرو بن عبيد بالفتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r14.claim: Abu ʿAmr rejects the damma reading.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r15.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash says he heard only the kasra form from Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r15.anchor: وقال الأخفش لم يسمع من العرب إلا الكسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r16.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r16.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says the damma form is the more common of the two.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r17.speaker: اليزيدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r17.claim: Al-Yazidi identifies kasra as the Hijazi dialect.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r18.claim: The three vowels may all be dialect variants; alternatively, fatḥa could be a verbal noun used as a place name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r18.anchor: فيحتمل أن تكون الثلاث لغى ويحتمل أن يكون الفتح مصدرا سمي به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r19.claim: The kasra and damma are also transmitted in a line by Aws, evidencing both pronunciations.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r20.claim: A reading العدية changes wāw to yāʾ because of the preceding kasra; the silent consonant does not block the change, as in صبية and قنية.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r20.anchor: بالعدية بقلب الواو لكسرة العين ولم يعتدوا بالساكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r21.claim: The Badr valley runs east from Medina; the battle site is two stages away, and the valley bends toward the nearby sea.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r21.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود بالعدوة العليا وهم بالعدوة السفلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r22.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r22.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads القصيا, the expected analogical form and a usage of Tamim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r22.anchor: ووادي بدر آخذين الشرق والقبلة منحرف إلى البحر الذي هو قريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r23.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r23.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading calls the two banks upper and lower, respectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p327/r23.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود بالعدوة العليا وهم بالعدوة السفلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r1.claim: The location of the battle site is east of Medina, two travel stages between them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r1.anchor: والمدينة من الوادي من موضع الوقعة منه في الشرق وبينهما مرحلتان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r2.claim: The best parse coordinates وهم and الركب with أنتم as subjects dividing the situations of the two sides; alternatively both waw letters mark circumstance, with أسفل as predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r2.anchor: والأحسن أن يكون وهم والركب معطوفان على أنتم فهي مبتدآت تقسيم لحالهم وحال أعدائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r3.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads أسفل in the nominative, extending the adverb’s use so it becomes the subject itself figuratively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي أسفل بالرفع اتسع في الظرف فجعله نفس المبتدأ مجازا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r4.claim: الركب may mean the forty men driving Abu Sufyan’s caravan, or the camels carrying the unbelievers’ provisions and belongings, kept in a safe place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r4.anchor: والركب هم الأربعون الذين كانوا يقودون العير عير أبي سفيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the positions show the enemy’s strength and readiness against the Muslims’ weakness, making their victory manifestly God’s doing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r5.anchor: الفائدة فيه الإخبار عن الحالة الدالة على قوة شأن العدو وشوكته وتكامل عدته وتمهد أسباب الغلبة له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r6.claim: The enemy held the higher bank with water and firm ground, while Muslims were on muddy terrain without water and struggled to walk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r6.anchor: العدوة القصوى التي أناخ بها المشركون كان فيها الماء وكانت أرضا لا بأس بها ولا ماء بالعدوة الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r7.claim: The caravan behind the enemy increased their resolve because people fought fiercely to protect their families and property rather than leave them behind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r7.anchor: وكانت العير وراء ظهور العدو مع كثرة عددهم وكانت الحماية دونها تضاعف حميتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Abu Sufyan, warned of the Prophet, had avoided Badr and taken the coastal route, so the caravan lay below relative to the upper valley.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: كان الركب ومدبر أمره أبو سفيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says Abu Sufyan’s Syrian trading party and Muhammad’s companions did not know the opposing Quraysh party was approaching until all met at Badr’s water, fought, and the Muslims captured them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: أقبل أبو سفيان وأصحابه من الشام تجارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r2.speaker: الطبري وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari and others say that if the parties had agreed to meet and then saw their disparity in numbers, they would have broken the appointment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r2.anchor: قال الطبري وغيره: المعنى لو تواعدتم على الاجتماع ثم علمتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says mutual fear would have kept the small Muslim force from keeping an agreed appointment, while the Quraysh feared the Prophet and his followers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r3.anchor: وقال معناه الزمخشري، قال: ولو تواعدتم أنتم وأهل مكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r4.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r4.claim: Al-Mahdawi explains that interruptions and obstacles would have kept the people from meeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r4.anchor: وقال المهدوي: المعنى لاختلفتم بالقواطع والعوارض القاطعة بالناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers al-Mahdawi’s explanation to al-Tabari’s: the passage highlights God’s favor and power in arranging Badr, which human efforts alone could not have achieved.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا أنبل يعني من قول الطبري وأصح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r6.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r6.claim: Al-Kirmani says an agreed battle would still have failed because the Quraysh would not trust the promise and would seek a ruse against the Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r6.anchor: وقال الكرماني ولو تواعدتم أنتم والمشركون للقتال لاختلفتم في الميعاد أي كانوا لا يصدقون مواعدتكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that without God’s decree the battle would not have occurred as planned, since He intended victory for His religion and humiliation for unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r7.anchor: وقيل المعنى ولو تواعدتم من غير قضاء الله أمر الحرب لاختلفتم في الميعاد ليقضي الله أمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r8.claim: كان مفعولا means an event that existed, was actual, and was certain to happen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ليقضي أمرا قد قدره في الأزل مفعولا لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says God had decreed the affair from eternity for it to occur when its appointed time arrived, all of which He already knew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ليقضي الله متعلق بمحذوف أي ليقضي الله أمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches ليقضي الله to an omitted clause: God arranged matters to fulfill what had to happen, the victory of His allies over His enemies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ليقضي الله متعلق بمحذوف أي ليقضي الله أمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r11.claim: Possible parses make ليهلك an appositive to ليقضي, attach it to مفعولا, or supply an omitted initial conjunction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r11.anchor: وقيل كان بمعنى صار ليهلك بدل من ليقضي فيتعلق بمثل ما تعلق به ليقضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r12.claim: The apparent sense is that those killed among Quraysh die with clear proof and the living remain with clear proof, leaving no excuse against the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق وغيره: ليكفر ويؤمن فالمعنى أن الله تعالى جعل قصة بدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r13.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r13.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others interpret the two outcomes as disbelief and belief: Badr became a clear sign through which people believed or disbelieved knowingly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: ليهلك بفتح اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r14.speaker: الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r14.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿIsma from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read ليهلك with fatḥa on the lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: ليهلك بفتح اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r15.claim: The cited line by al-Mutalammis demonstrates the separated pronunciation; separation and assimilation are both well-known linguistic forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ نافع والبزي وأبو بكر من حيي بالفك وباقي السبعة بالإدغام وقال المتلمس:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r16.speaker: نافع والبزي وأبو بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r16.claim: Nafiʿ, al-Bazzi, and Abu Bakr read حيي with separated consonants; the other seven readers assimilate them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p328#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ نافع والبزي وأبو بكر من حيي بالفك وباقي السبعة بالإدغام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r1.claim: The closing attributes hear speech and know intentions because disbelief and belief involve spoken words and inward conviction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r1.anchor: لأن الكفر والإيمان يستلزمان النطق اللساني والاعتقاد الجناني فهو سميع لأقوالكم عليم بنياتكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r12.claim: The cited al-Mutalammis line demonstrates the separated pronunciation; separation and assimilation are both well-known linguistic forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p329/r12.anchor: فهذا أوان العرض حي ذبابه والفك والإدغام لغتان مشهورتان

TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r3.claim: A report in al-ʿAyyāshī identifies the caravan below the Muslims as Abū Sufyān and his companions.
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r3.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن محمد بن يحيى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { والركب أسفل منكم } قال أبو سفيان وأصحابه.

TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r4.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r4.claim: On the statement about the one who perishes or lives by clear proof, al-Qummī says those who remain will know that God gave him victory.
TABATABAI:8:41-54#5/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة } الآية قال قال يعلم من بقي أن الله نصره.

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r1.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes إذ governed by an understood اذكروا.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه منصوب ب " اذكروا " مقدرا وهو قول الزجاج

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r2.claim: A second analysis makes إذ an appositive of يوم الفرقان.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه بدل من " يوم الفرقان " أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r3.claim: A third analysis governs إذ by قدير, but God's attribute of power is not restricted to a time.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنه منصوب ب " قدير " ، وهذا ليس بواضح، إذ لا يتقيد اتصافه بالقدرة

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r4.claim: A fourth analysis attaches إذ to الفرقان: the event distinguished truth and falsehood when the believers were at the valley bank.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنه منصوب بالفرقان أي: فرق بين الحق والباطل

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r5.claim: بالعدوة attaches to an omitted predicate as the subject's predicate; bāʾ means في, as in زيد بمكة.

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read kasra on ʿayn in both occurrences; the others use damma. Both forms mean a valley's bank or edge.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالعدوة بكسر العين فيهما. والباقون بالضم فيهما وهما لغتان

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r7.claim: The name is explained from عدا: the bank restrains water in the valley from passing beyond it.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r7.anchor: سميت بذلك لأنها عدت ما في الوادي من ماء ونحوه أن يتجاوزها أي منعته

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r8.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r8.claim: The cited poem's عدتني witnesses the root sense of keeping back or preventing passage.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: 2421 عدتني عن زيارتها العوادي

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r9.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي وقتادة وعمرو بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r9.claim: Al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Ali, Qatada, and Amr ibn Ubayd read with fatḥa; most linguists treat all three vowels as synonymous dialects.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وقتادة وعمرو بن عبيد بالفتح، وهي كلها لغات بمعنى واحد

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء والأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r10.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and al-Akhfash reject damma and say only kasra is attested; Abu Ubayd transmits both and calls damma more common.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r10.anchor: على أن أبا عمرو بن العلاء أنكر الضم ووافقه الأخفش فقال: " لم يسمع من العرب إلا الكسر "

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r11.speaker: اليزيدي
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r11.claim: Al-Yazidi calls kasra a Hijazi dialect and adduces Aws ibn Hajar's use of عدوته with kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r11.anchor: وقال اليزيدي: " الكسر لغة الحجاز " وأنشد قول أوس بن حجر:

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r12.claim: The author rejects denying kasra or damma because both are mass-transmitted readings, and suggests Abu Amr had not heard the other.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r12.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ينبغي أن يقال فلا وجه لإنكار الضم ولا الكسر لتواتر كل منهما

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r13.claim: The fatḥa reading may be a verbal noun used as a place name.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال في قراءة من قرأ بفتح

SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r14.speaker: قارئ
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r14.claim: An anomalous reading has العدِيَة, changing wāw to yāʾ after kasra; the intervening quiescent consonant does not block the change, as in دنيا, قنية, and صبية.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42/r14.anchor: وقرئ شاذا " بالعدية " بقلب الواو ياء لانكسار ما تقدمها، ولا يعتبر الفاصل لأنه ساكن

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r1.claim: القصوى is the feminine of الأقصى, meaning farther; قصو means distance.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { القصوى } تأنيث الأقصى. والأقصى: الأبعد. والقصو: البعد.

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r2.claim: The prevalent account changes wāw to yāʾ in feminine فعلى nouns, as in الدنيا, العليا, and القصيا; these forms were originally adjectives but became noun-like.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r2.anchor: وللتصريفيين عبارتان أغلبهما أن فعلى من ذوات الواو: إن كانت اسما أبدلت لامها ياء

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r3.claim: On that account, true adjectives retain wāw, as الحلوى; القصوى is irregular by analogy though Hijazi, while القصيا is regular and Tamimi.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r3.anchor: قالوا: وإن كانت فعلى صفة أقرت لامها على حالها نحو: الحلوى تأنيث الأحلى

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r4.claim: Yaqub ibn al-Sikkit calls القصوى anomalous; al-Zamakhshari compares its retention of wāw to القود and says القصوى is more frequent than القصيا.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r4.anchor: وممن نص على شذوذ القصوى يعقوب بن السكيت. وقال الزمخشري:

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads بالعدوة والقصيا, the Tamimi form considered analogical under the first account.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r5.anchor: وقد قرأ زيد بن علي " بالعدوة والقصيا " فجاء بها على لغة تميم، وهي القياس

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r6.claim: A less common reversed account says adjectives change wāw to yāʾ, while nouns retain it, as حزوى in a cited poem.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r6.anchor: والعبارة الثانية وهي المغلوبة القليلة العكس، أي: إن كانت صفة أبدلت نحو: العليا والدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r7.claim: Under the reversed account, الحلوى and القصوى are irregular because they are adjectives that retain wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا فالحلوى شاذة لإقرار لامها مع كونها صفة، وكذا القصوى أيضا عند هؤلاء

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r8.claim: Both accounts make القصوى irregular by analogy and القصيا regular; they differ on الحلوى and حزوى. Anomaly here means irregularity of analogy, not rare usage, since القصوى is mass-transmitted.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r8.anchor: وقد ترتب على هاتين العبارتين أن " قصوى " على خلاف القياس فيهما، وأن " قصيا " هي القياس

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r9.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r9.claim: The cited line أدارا بحزوى uses the noun example in the grammatical rule's discussion.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#2/r9.anchor: كقوله: 2423 أدارا بحزوى هجت للعين عبرة

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r1.claim: The better analysis makes both waw clauses coordinate with أنتم, beginning a division of the believers' and enemy's situations; both may instead be circumstantial clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r1.anchor: الأحسن في هذه الواو، والواو التي قبلها الداخلة

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r2.claim: أسفل is an adverb in place of the predicate and describes an omitted location lower than the believers' location.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r2.anchor: و " أسفل " منصوب على الظرف النائب عن الخبر، وهو في الحقيقة صفة لظرف مكان محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads أسفل nominative by extension, making the adverb the caravan; the author finds the standard analysis more emphatic.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " أسفل " بالرفع وذلك على سبيل الاتساع، جعل الظرف نفس الركب

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r4.speaker: الفراء والأخفش والكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ, al-Akhfash, and al-Kisaʾi allow nominative with an omitted موضع الركب; the author prefers the adverb analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r4.anchor: وأجاز الفراء والأخفش والكسائي " أسفل " بالرفع على تقدير محذوف أي: موضع الركب أسفل

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r5.claim: الركب is a collective singular meaning rider, not a broken plural as al-Akhfash says; the diminutive ركيبا preserves its form.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#3/r5.anchor: خلافا للأخفش لقوله: 2424 بنيته من عصبة من ماليا أخشى ركيبا أو رجيلا غاديا

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r1.claim: ليقضي attaches to an omitted phrase: you met so that God could decide the matter.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r1.anchor: قوله: { ولكن ليقضي } " ليقضي " متعلق بمحذوف، أي: ولكن تلاقيتم ليقضي

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies the purpose as victory for God's allies and defeat of His enemies, a matter He had to enact and arranged.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r2.anchor: وقدّر الزمخشري ذلك المحذوف فقال: " أي: ليقضي الله أمرا كان واجبا أن يفعل وهو نصر أوليائه

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r3.claim: كان may retain its past-time sense or mean صار, marking a transition from unrealized to accomplished.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r3.anchor: و " كان " يحتمل أن تكون على بابها من الدلالة على اقتران مضمون الجملة بالزمان الماضي

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r4.claim: One analysis makes ليهلك an appositive to ليقضي, repeating its governing lām.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r4.anchor: أحدها: أنه بدل من قوله " ليقضي " بإعادة العامل فيتعلق بما تعلق به الأول

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r5.claim: Another analysis attaches ليهلك to مفعولا, explaining the purpose for which the matter was done.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنه متعلق بقوله " مفعولا " ، أي: فعل هذا الأمر لكيت وكيت

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r6.claim: A third analysis coordinates ليهلك with ليقضي after an omitted conjunction, a very rare deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r6.anchor: الثالث: أنه متعلق بما تعلق به " ليقضي " على سبيل العطف عليه بحرف عطف محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches ليهلك directly to يقضي.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r7.anchor: الرابع: أنه متعلق ب " يقضي " ذكره أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r8.speaker: الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿIsma from Abu Bakr from Asim read ليهلك with fatḥa on lām; common usage supports that form, as in 4:176 and 40:34.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم " ليهلك " بفتح اللام، وقياس ماضي هذا " هلك " بالكسر

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر والبزي
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r1.claim: Nafi, Abu Bakr from Asim, and al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir pronounce the yāʾs distinctly in حيّ; the other readers assimilate them.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع، وأبو بكر عن عاصم، والبزي عن ابن كثير بالإظهار، والباقون بالإدغام

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r2.claim: Both pronunciations are established dialects in past verbs ending in two yāʾs, the first kasra, such as حيي and عيي.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r2.anchor: والإظهار والإدغام في هذا النوع لغتان مشهورتان: وهو كل ما آخره ياءان من الماضي

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r3.speaker: المتلمس
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r3.claim: Al-Mutalammis's line فهذا أوان العرض حي ذبابه attests assimilation in حيّ.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r3.anchor: ومن الإدغام قول المتلمس: 2425 فهذا أوان العرض حي ذبابه

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r4.speaker: آخر
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r4.claim: An anonymous poet's عيوا بأمرهم كما عيت ببيضتها الحمامه attests assimilation in عيوا.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r4.anchor: وقال آخر: 2426 عيوا بأمرهم كما عيت ببيضتها الحمامه

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r5.claim: Distinct pronunciation preserves the original form, avoids doubling a weak letter, follows the imperfect where the second yāʾ becomes alif, and reflects a disappearing or different vowel; Sibawayh reports it from Yunus and heard forms like أحيياء.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r5.anchor: فمن أظهر فلأنه الأصل، ولأن الإدغام يؤدي إلى تضعيف حرف العلة وهو ثقيل في ذاته،

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r6.claim: Assimilation avoids a heavy kasra on a matching consonant; the second vowel is fixed as a morphological vowel, and its loss in حييت does not prevent assimilation, like حللت and ظللت.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r6.anchor: ومن أدغم فلاستثقال ظهر الكسرة في حرف يجانسه؛ ولأن حركة الثانية لازمة لأنها حركة بناء،

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r7.claim: These arguments concern the past with a building vowel; when the second yāʾ has an inflectional vowel, only distinct pronunciation occurs, as in يحيي and لن يعيي.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#5/r7.anchor: وهذا كله فيما كانت حركته حركة بناء، ولذلك قيد به بالماضي، أما إذا كانت حركة إعراب

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r1.claim: عن بينة attaches to both يهلك and يحيا.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r1.anchor: قوله: { عن بينة }: متعلق ب " يهلك " و " يحيا "

SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r2.claim: Death and life mean disbelief and faith: each state should issue from clear evidence, not uncertainty or a misleading doubt.
SAMIN-DURR:8:42#6/r2.anchor: والهلاك والحياة عبارة عن الإيمان والكفر. والمعنى: ليصدر كفر من كفر عن وضوح وبيان

ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r7.claim: The description of the two camps' locations further clarifies the decisive contrast in God's aid at Badr.
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r7.anchor: فقال عز وجل: (إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى

ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r8.claim: Al-dunyā is the nearer side; al-ʿidwa is a valley bank, with the banks located toward Medina and Mecca.
ZAJJAJ:v2p416/r8.anchor: أي الدنيا منكم، والعدوة شفير الوادي

ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r1.claim: The farther bank was the edge of the valley on the Mecca side.

ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r2.claim: Al-rakb is the caravan led by Abu Sufyan, which was on the seashore.
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r2.anchor: الركب: العير التي كان فيها أبو سفيان على شاطئ البحر

ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r3.claim: Muslims faced sinking sand and no water, while the better-positioned polytheists had water and guarded the caravan; victory despite their smaller numbers and weaker position made God's aid a decisive distinction.
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r3.anchor: وكان المشركون نازلين على موضع فيه الماء، وهم مع ذلك يحامون عن العير، فهو أشد لشوكتهم

ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p417/r4.claim: The recited accusative makes the caravan a place lower than you; a permissible nominative instead predicates that the caravan is lower or farther down.

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r1.claim: God makes the seeker of truth like a living person and the misguided like one who has perished.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r1.anchor: جعل الله عز وجل القاصد للحق بمنزلة الحي، وجعل الضال بمنزلة الهالك

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r2.claim: Both ḥayiya with two explicit yāʾs and ḥayya with an assimilated doubled yāʾ are reported readings.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r2.anchor: ويجوز حيي بياءين، وحي بياء مشددة مدغمة، وقد قرئ بهما جميعا

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r3.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r3.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh permit either assimilation or clear pronunciation when the second vowel is fixed; assimilation joins like letters, while clear pronunciation reflects the changed form of the second yāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r3.anchor: فأما الخليل وسيبويه فيجيزان الإدغام والإظهار إذا كانت الحركة في الثاني لازمة

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r4.claim: Clear pronunciation is supported by the forms ḥayiya yaḥyā, al-maḥyā, and al-mamāt.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r4.anchor: وأما من أظهر فلأن الحرف الثاني ينتقل عن لفظ الياء، تقول حيي يحيا، والمحيا والممات

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r5.claim: For yuhyī and the verse about reviving the dead, Basran grammarians unanimously require two clear yāʾs; some others allow a single assimilated yāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r5.anchor: فلا يجوز فيه عند جميع البصريين إلا يحيي بياءين ظاهرتين

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r6.claim: Zajjaj rejects an anonymous anomalous poem as evidence for assimilation, since its poet and tribe are unknown and the Quran must not rest on an unidentified recitation or a stray verse.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r6.anchor: وليس ينبغي أن يحمل كتاب الله على " أنشدني بعضهم " ولا على بيت شاذ

ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r7.claim: Even for non-weak consonants such as in lam yawad, clear gemination is preferred when the second letter would be still; a weak final letter gives no stronger case for assimilation.
ZAJJAJ:v2p418/r7.anchor: نحو: " لم يود " فالاختيار إظهار التضعيف

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r1.claim: At Badr, the Prophet and his followers camped at the valley's northern end nearest Medina, while the Meccans occupied its southern end.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r1.anchor: the Prophet and his followers were encamped in the northern part of the valley of Badr, nearest to Medina

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r2.claim: The caravan was Abu Sufyan's Meccan trade caravan from Syria, traveling south through the coastal lowlands.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n43/r2.anchor: The Meccan trade caravan, coming from Syria under the leadership of Abu Sufyan, was in the meantime proceeding southwards through the coastal lowlands

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r1.claim: Asad freely expands the elliptical conditional: had they arranged a battle appointment, they would have failed to keep it.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r1.anchor: a very free rendering of the elliptic phrase which runs, literally, thus

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r2.claim: Most followers expected to meet the relatively weak trade caravan, and some were dismayed to face the powerful Quraysh army instead.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n44/r2.anchor: most of the Prophet's followers had been under the impression that their objective was the relatively weak trade caravan

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r1.speaker: all commentators
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r1.claim: All commentators take Asad's bracketed additions as implied by the highly elliptical sentence.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r1.anchor: According to all the commentators, the words interpolated by me between brackets are implied

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r2.claim: A decree of God must inevitably come to pass, so the verse can describe it as already done.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n45/r2.anchor: meaning that if God decrees a thing, it must inevitably come about

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r1.speaker: Some of the great commentators
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r1.claim: Some major commentators read destruction as continued denial of truth and life as faith, metaphorically.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r1.anchor: Some of the great commentators understand this sentence in a metaphorical sense

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r2.speaker: Ibn Ishaq
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq, quoted by Ibn Kathir, reads the phrase as allowing deniers to persist in denial and believers in belief after clear evidence.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r2.anchor: Ibn Ishaq, as quoted by Ibn Kathir

ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r3.claim: Asad prefers the literal deaths and survival of Badr's participants: fallen believers knew themselves martyrs, survivors saw God's hand in victory, and defeated deniers saw the futility or cause of their defeat.
ASAD-NOTES:8:42#n46/r3.anchor: In my opinion, however, it is preferable to interpret the references to death and life in their prima-facie (that is, not metaphorical) sense

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p47.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p47.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p47.claim: Although the sūrah's address appears general, Islahi says it is directed particularly to the group of weak Muslims.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p47.anchor: though the apparently the address in the whole of this sūrah is general, yet it is directed towards the group of weak Muslims.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.claim: The Badr scene exemplifies the divine planning mentioned in the preceding verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.anchor: This verse depicts an example of God’s planning that was referred to in the previous verse.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.claim: God’s guidance brought the Prophet and Quraysh to Badr at the same time: the Prophet had been shown the caravan and army in a dream, then arrived as Quraysh came under the pretext of protecting the caravan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.anchor: valley of Badr right at the time when on the opposite side the army of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.claim: Timely arrival can determine a battle: delay risks defeat, arriving early brings danger, and Muslim supply problems made timing especially sensitive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.anchor: Even a slight delay, at times can result in defeat.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.claim: God protected the Muslims from military stratagems; an army’s declaration or ultimatum may conceal its true target, and prior coordination would not readily have produced this meeting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p51.anchor: The planning behind the declaration of war and giving ultimatum to the enemy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.claim: God’s special planning made the believers meet their enemy so that the destined event would take place.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.anchor: God through His special planning made the believers face their enemy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.claim: The verse’s death and life refer to spiritual death and life: the decisive encounter brings people to belief or disbelief with the proof made manifest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.anchor: Death and life are referred to here in the spiritual sense.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.claim: The Arabic preposition bi can mark the source or origin of something.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.anchor: delineating the source and origin of something.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.claim: Badr became a decisive proof between believers and disbelievers: the disbelievers had no excuse and the believers no ambiguity, with each side’s reality plain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.anchor: The battle of Badr had become such a decisive event

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.claim: God’s hearing and knowledge encompass the entire unlikely arrangement, including hidden plans and inward whispers, by which He brought each party to the place for His intended result.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p52.anchor: He made each of them reach the right place

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p58.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p58.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p58.claim: Islahi compares Badr’s layout, number of fighters, and objective with Israel’s battle under Saul against Goliath in Samuel’s time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p58.anchor: Badr with regard to its battle-layout, number of fighters and objective of the battle was similar to the one fought by the Israelites under Saul

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read both occurrences of العدوة with kasra on ʿayn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: بالعدوة*، وبالعدوة* العين فيهما مكسورة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r2.claim: These readers use ḍamma on ʿayn in both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بضم العين فيهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن ويونس
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says kasra is the Arabic form he heard, and reports it as Abū ʿAmr’s and ʿĪsā’s reading; Yūnus says he heard it from Arabs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: تقرأ بالكسر، وهو كلام العرب

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r4.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r4.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā says ḍamma is the more common of the two dialects; Abū ʿUbayda calls both dialects and says ḍamma predominates in recitation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p128#2/r4.anchor: قال أحمد بن يحيى: الضم في العدوة أكثر اللغتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r1.speaker: ابن كثير في رواية قنبل وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r1.claim: These readers assimilate the two yāʾs into one geminated yāʾ in حي; Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim also has one yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير في رواية قنبل، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: من حي عن بينة بياء واحدة مشددة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r2.speaker: البزي عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r2.claim: Al-Bazzī’s transmission from Ibn Kathīr and the transmissions of Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ retain two yāʾs, the first kasra and the second fatḥa; a Shibl report from Ibn Kathīr agrees.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r2.anchor: وقال البزي عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير: حيي عن بينة بياءين، الأولى مكسورة والثانية مفتوحة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r3.claim: Assimilation is justified because the yāʾ is vowelled and so resembles a sound consonant; unlike a quiescent yāʾ, it is not deleted in connected or paused forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير في رواية قنبل، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: من حي عن بينة بياء واحدة مشددة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r4.claim: Al-Fārisī treats حي as a verbal noun meaning life, like العي; sources are generally not pluralized, and a plural on فعل would be expected to show both ḍamma and kasra variants.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r4.anchor: أبو عبيدة: الحياة والحيوان، والحي واحد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r5.speaker: محمد بن السري عن بعض أهل اللغة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r5.claim: A linguist cited by Muḥammad ibn al-Sarrī reads Umayya’s حية as meaning حياة, analogous to ʿayb/ʿāb and similar forms, rather than the exceptional pattern of آية and غاية.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p129/r5.anchor: وذكر محمد بن السري أن بعض أهل اللغة قال في قول أمية

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r1.claim: In the vocabulary of hoofs, حي names the part that remains alive at the bottom while other parts are described as dead there because they do not remain in that place.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r1.anchor: ومعنى حي في الأكارع: حي في أسفل الأكارع، وأسفل الأكارع: الخف

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r2.claim: Abū Zayd cites the idiom حي خويلد in a line, where حي is used in reference to a person.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r2.anchor: وأنشد أبو زيد : يا قر إن أباك حي خويلد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن وأحمد بن إبراهيم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan’s line uses حي before Abū al-Mughīra, and Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm reports حي بكر where حي likewise stands with a personal or tribal name.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r3.anchor: وأنشد أبو الحسن : أبو بحر أشد الناس منا ...

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r4.claim: Idghām is possible because the yāʾ has a vowel and thus behaves like a sound consonant; the comparison with deleted yāʾs in declension shows why the moving yāʾ is retained.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p138/r4.anchor: فلأن الياء قد لزمتها الحركة وصارت بلزوم الحركة لها مشابهة للصحيح

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r1.claim: The author defends a reading that coordinates honey and water without the definite article: they are kinds, effectively meaning the honey and the water; this avoids al-Aʿmash's charge of vulgarity or solecism.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r1.anchor: إنه إنما جاز ذلك من حيث كان عسل وماء هما جنسين، فكأنه قال: يكون مزاجها العسل والماء،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r2.claim: The poem كأن سبيئة من بيت رأس is evidence for the coordinated generic nouns عسل وماء.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r2.anchor: كأن سبيئة من بيت رأس ... يكون مزاجها عسل وماء2

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن وعمرو
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r3.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, and ʿAmr read بالعدوة, with reports differing among them; the author treats this as a third dialect beside the two common vowelings.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r3.anchor: وقرأ: "بالعدوة" قتادة2 والحسن3 وعمرو، واختلف عنهم.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r4.claim: The three dialectal forms of عدوة parallel variants such as رغوة, صفوة, عشوة, حضرة, غشوة, غلظة, لجبة, ربوة, and مدية.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r4.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: الذي في هذا أنها لغة ثالثة، كقولهم: في اللبن رغوة ورغوة ورغوة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r5.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads فشرذ بهم من خلفهم with ذāl instead of dāl; because no root sh-r-d is known, the author explains ذ as a substitute for the similar voiced د, as in خرادل/خراذل.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك ما يروى عن الأعمش أنه قرأ: "فشرذ بهم من خلفهم "7 بالذال معجمة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r6.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r6.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads فاجنح لها with ḍamma on nūn; Sibawayh records جنح يجنح, while the author says ḍamma is more analogical for this intransitive verb.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الأشهب العقيلي: "فاجنح لها"9 بضم النون.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r7.claim: For intransitives, يفعل is the more analogical pattern, as قعد يقعد; يفعل is normally associated with transitive verbs, so ضرب يضرب is more regular than قتل يقتل.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p279/r7.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: حكى سيبويه جنح يجنح، وهي في طريق ركد يركد، وقعد يقعد،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r1.claim: The two-yāʾ reading preserves the verb's original form, with first yāʾ kasra and second fatḥa.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r1.anchor: يقرأ بياءين الأولى مكسورة والثانية مفتوحة وبياء واحدة شديدة مفتوحة فالحجة لمن قرأه بياءين أنه أتى به على الأصل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r2.claim: The one doubled yāʾ assimilates two moving yāʾs that are heavy to pronounce together.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p171/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن أدغم أنه استثقل اجتماع ياءين متحركتين فأسكن الأولى وأدغمها في الثانية

NASHR:v2p275/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p275/r10.speaker: المدنيان وابن عامر
NASHR:v2p275/r10.claim: The two Medinans and Ibn ʿĀmir read the hamza in وإن الله with fatḥa; the others use kasra.
NASHR:v2p275/r10.anchor: وإن الله فقرأ المدنيان، وابن عامر بفتح الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بكسرها

NASHR:v2p275/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p275/r12.speaker: ابن كثير والبصريان
NASHR:v2p275/r12.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the two Basran readers use kasra on the ʿayn in both occurrences of العدوة.
NASHR:v2p275/r12.anchor: في الموضعين فقرأ ابن كثير، والبصريان بكسر العين فيهما

NASHR:v2p275/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p275/r13.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p275/r13.claim: All remaining readers use ḍamma on the ʿayn in both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p275/r13.anchor: والبصريان بكسر العين فيهما، وقرأ الباقون بضم فيهما

NASHR:v2p275/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p275/r14.speaker: المدنيان ويعقوب وخلف والبزي وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p275/r14.claim: These readers pronounce two distinct yāʾs in من حيّ, the first with kasra and the second with fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p275/r14.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان ويعقوب وخلف والبزي وأبو بكر بياءين ظاهرتين الأولى مكسورة

NASHR:v2p275/r15.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p275/r15.speaker: ابن شنبوذ والزينبي وابن مجاهد
NASHR:v2p275/r15.claim: Qunbul’s transmission differs: Ibn Shanabūdh and al-Zaynabī report two yāʾs, while Ibn Mujāhid reports one geminated yāʾ; al-Dānī calls Ibn Mujāhid’s attribution an error because his own books conflict.
NASHR:v2p275/r15.anchor: واختلف عن قنبل، فروى عنه ابن شنبوذ كذلك بياءين، وكذا روى عنه الزينبي

QIRAAT-ER:8:42:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:4#1/r1.claim: The kasra variant ʿidwa alongside standard ʿudwa is a dialectal vowel alternation; both mean valley-bank.
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:4#1/r1.anchor: Kasra on ʿayn (ʿidwa instead of ʿudwa) — dialectal variant of the same word

QIRAAT-ER:8:42:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:9#1/r1.claim: The same kasra variant at the second occurrence applies to both occurrences of ʿudwa.
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:9#1/r1.anchor: Same kasra variant as word 4 — applies identically to both occurrences of ʿudwa

QIRAAT-ER:8:42:39#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:39#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:39#1/r1.claim: The unassimilated ḥayiya keeps the two yāʾs separate instead of geminating them; both forms are canonical seven-reader readings.
QIRAAT-ER:8:42:39#1/r1.anchor: Unassimilated form — ḥayiya instead of ḥayya; the two yāʾs are kept separate rather than geminated

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p259#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p259#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p259#4/r1.claim: Qatada locates the Muslims at the near bank of the valley, the enemy at the far bank, and Abu Sufyan’s caravan below them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p259#4/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا ﴾ قال شقير الوادي الأدنى وهم بشفير الوادي الأقصى

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r1.claim: Idh is either an appositive to “the day” or governed by an understood “remember”; Abū al-Baqāʾ's attachment to qadīr is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r1.anchor: بدل من يوم أو معمول لاذكروا مقدرا وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون ظرفا لقدير وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r2.claim: Al-ʿudwah means a side or bank of a valley, from ʿadw, crossing or going beyond.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r2.anchor: والعدوة بالحركات الثلاث شط الوادي وأصله من العدو التجاوز

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r3.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on ʿudwah; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb read it with kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r3.anchor: والقراءة المشهورة الضم والكسر وهو قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو ويعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and others read ʿudwah with fatḥa; all three vowelings are dialect forms despite objections to some.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وغيرهما بالفتح وكلها لغات بمعنى ولا عبرة بإنكار بعضها

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r5.claim: Al-dunyā is the feminine of al-adnā, the nearer bank to Medina.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r5.anchor: تأنيث الأدنى أي إذ أنتم نازلون بشفير الوادي الأقرب إلى المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r6.claim: Al-quṣwā is the feminine of al-aqṣā, the farther bank from Medina; “they” refers to the polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r6.anchor: أي المشركون ( بالعدوة القصوى ( أي البعدى من المدينة وهو تأنيث الأقصى

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r7.anchor: زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( القصيا ) ومن قواعدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r8.claim: The usual rule changes the final wāw of feminine faʿlā nouns from roots with wāw to yāʾ, as dunyā does; quṣwā retains wāw because it is originally an adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r8.anchor: ومن قواعدهم أن فعلى من ذوات الواو إذا كان اسما تبدل لامه ياء كدنيا فإنه من دنا يدنو إذا قرب

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r9.claim: If quṣwā is treated as a lexicalized noun, qaṣiyā is also recorded: it is Tamīmī, while quṣwā is Ḥijāzī.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r9.anchor: وأنه جرى مجرى الأسماء الجامدة قيل قصيا وهي لغة تميم والأولى لغة أهل الحجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r10.speaker: من أهل التصريف
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r10.claim: Some morphologists state the reverse dominant rule: adjectives change final wāw, nouns preserve it, making quṣwā anomalous by analogy but not in usage or eloquence.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r10.anchor: من أهل التصريف من قال : إن اللغة الغالبة العكس فإن كانت صفة أبدلت اللام نحو العليا

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r11.claim: The form is anomalous only for departing from analogy, not usage or eloquence; competing explanations cite adjective weight and the noun-adjective distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r11.anchor: وعنوا بالشذوذ مخالفة القياس لا الاستعمال فلا تنافي الفصاحة وذكروا في تعليل عدم الإبدال بالفرق

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r12.claim: Al-rakb means the caravan or its riders, Abū Sufyān and companions; correctly analyzed, it is a collective noun rather than a plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r12.anchor: أي العير أو أصحابها أبو سفيان وأصحابه وهو اسم جمع راكب لا جمع على الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r13.claim: The caravan was below the Muslims' position, on the seashore; as a locative accusative it stands for the place and remains descriptive.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r13.anchor: أي في مكان أسفل من مكانكم يعني ساحل البحر وهو نصب على الظرفية وفي الأصل صفة للظرف

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r14.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash allow nominative by expansion or with an implied “the caravan's place is below.”
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r14.anchor: وأجاز الفراء والأخفش رفعه على الاتساع أو بتقدير موضع الركب أسفل

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r15.claim: The caravan clause coordinates with the clause governed by idh; most take it as a circumstantial clause attached to the preceding prepositional phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r15.anchor: الجملة عطف على مدخول إذ أي إذ أنتم الخ وإذ الركب الخ + واختار الجمهور أنها في موضع الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r16.claim: The extended scene-setting depicts God's plan at Badr, His favor, and the event as a manifest sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r16.anchor: يوم الفرقان يوم النصر والظفر على الأعداء مثلا تصوير ما دبر سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the timing, locations, and caravan position show the enemy's strength and preparation against Muslim weakness, so victory could only be God's work and power.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r17.anchor: وهذا مراد الزمخشري بقوله فائدة هذا التوقيت وذكر مراكز الفريقين

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r18.claim: The polytheists occupied the bank with water and firm ground, while the Muslims' nearer bank was waterless, soft terrain where feet sank; the caravan lay behind the enemy.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r18.anchor: العدوة القصوى التي أناخ بها المشركون كان فيها الماء وكانت أرضا لا بأس بها

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r19.claim: With their larger numbers and the caravan to protect, the enemy had heightened zeal and determination to hold position; Muslim victory in these conditions displayed divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r19.anchor: وكانت العير وراء ظهر العدو مع كثرة عددهم فكانت الحماية دونها تضاعف حميتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r20.claim: The point is not why already-known facts were reported, answered by saying their benefit was merely inherent; that framing misses the passage's portrayal of the event.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r20.anchor: ليس السؤال عن فائدة الإخبار بما هو معلوم للمخاطب ليكون الجواب بأن فائدته لازمة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r21.claim: If Muslims and Meccans had agreed to meet knowing their conditions, the Muslims would have failed the appointment from fear and despair.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r21.anchor: أي لو تواعدتم أنتم وهم القتال وعلمتم حالهم وحالكم لاختلفتم أنتم في الميعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r22.claim: The first pronoun includes both sides by grammatical predominance, while the second is restricted to Muslims, fitting the emphasis on their weakness and God's aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r22.anchor: وجعل الضمير الأول شاملا للجمعين تغليبا والثاني للمسلمين خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r23.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r23.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes both pronouns to include both sides: numbers would deter the Muslims, while fear of the Prophet and believers would deter Meccans, preventing an arranged battle.

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r24.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds al-Zamakhsharī's uniform-pronoun reading unsuitable; pronoun shifts are easy, and the armies met without an appointment.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r24.anchor: وأمر التفكيك سهل ولكن تلاقيتم على غير موعد

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r25.claim: The matter God was to bring about was the believers' victory and the enemies' defeat.

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r26.claim: Kāna mafʿūlan means it was bound to be done, either by the promise to help believers (30:47) or because it was decreed eternally.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r26.anchor: كان واجبا أن يفعل بسبب الوعد المشار إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r27.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r27.claim: Another view takes kāna as ṣāra, “became”: the matter came to be done after not yet being done.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r27.anchor: وقيل : كان بمعنى صار الدالة على التحول أي صار مفعولا

ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r28.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r28.claim: The purpose clause may replace li-yaqḍiya with the preposition repeated, or attach to mafʿūlan.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p6#2/r28.anchor: بدل من ( ليقضي ) بإعادة الحرف أو متعلق بمفعولا

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also attaches the purpose clause to yaqḍī, and al-Ālūsī approves this first option.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r1.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أيضا تعلقه بيقضي واستطيب الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r2.claim: Bayyina is clear proof: whoever dies or lives does so on witnessed evidence, leaving no excuse; Badr itself was a manifest sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r2.anchor: والمراد بالبينة الحجة الظاهرة أي ليموت من يموت عن حجة عاينها

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r3.speaker: قتادة ومحمد بن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r3.claim: Qatāda and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq take life as faith and death as disbelief, figuratively or metonymically; God's decisive power makes belief or disbelief follow clear proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالحياة الإيمان وبالموت الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r4.claim: Another view takes those who perish or live as approaching death or life, or as destined for those outcomes in God's knowledge; approaching life means persisting after the battle.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r4.anchor: قيل : والمراد بمن هلك ومن حي المشارف للهلاك والحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r5.claim: One analysis takes ʿan as “after,” citing 54:26; past and future can mark what is impending relative to the event or decreed by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن ( عن ) بمعنى بعد كقوله تعالى : ( عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r6.claim: Taking the past relative to God's knowledge and decree and the future relative to outward events avoids difficulty; “life” means persistence, not merely being alive, or it would include those who perish.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r6.anchor: واعتبار المضي بالنظر إلى علم الله تعالى وقضائه والاستقبال بالنظر إلى الوجود الخارجي مما لا غبار عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r7.claim: ʿAn need not mean “after”: it can retain the Basran sense of separation, or mean “on/against,” as in 9:34 and a verse by Dhū al-Aṣbaʿ.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r7.anchor: و ( عن ) لا يتعين كونها بمعنى بعد بل يمكن أن تبقى على معنى المجاوزة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r8.speaker: ذي الأصبع
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r8.claim: Dhū al-Aṣbaʿ's line illustrates ʿan with the sense “over/against.”
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r8.anchor: قول ذي الأصبع : لاه ابن عمك لا أفضلت في حسب عني

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r9.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads li-yahlaka with fatḥa; it is also transmitted from ʿĀṣim.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r9.anchor: الأعمش ( ليهلك ) بفتح العين وروي ذلك عن عاصم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r10.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r10.claim: Ibn Jinnī calls this reading anomalous and undesirable because yafaʿalu normally requires a guttural middle or final consonant; al-Qāmūs records variant forms that permit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p7/r10.anchor: ابن جني في المحتسب شاذة مرغوب عنها لأن الماضي هلك بالفتح ولا يأتي فعل يفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r1.claim: The usual past is open-vowel halaka and the present has kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r1.anchor: نعم المشهور في الماضي الفتح وفي المضارع الكسر

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو بكر ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr, and Yaʿqūb read ḥayiya with the two yāʾs unassimilated.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r2.anchor: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو بكر ويعقوب ( حيي ) بفك الإدغام

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ gives two explanations: analogy with the present yahyā, or different vowels on the two radicals functioning like different consonants.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r3.anchor: وفيه وجهان أحدهما الحمل على المستقبل وهو يحيى فكما لم يدغم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r4.claim: The second vowel is temporary, so the second yāʾ is effectively treated as still; this supports nonassimilation, as in the optional ḍabab al-balad form.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r4.anchor: ويقوي ذلك أن الحركة الثانية عارضة فكأن الياء الثانية ساكنة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r5.claim: The two yāʾs in ḥayiya are original; the wāw in ḥayawān replaces yāʾ, while ḥiwāʾ belongs to ḥ-w-y, “gather,” not to ḥayya, “snake.”
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r5.anchor: واليا آن أصل وليست الثانية بدلا من واو وأما الحيوان فالواو فيه بدل من الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r6.claim: God hears the disbelievers' disbelief and knows their punishment, and hears believers' faith and knows their reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r6.anchor: أي بكفر من كفر وعقابه وإيمان من آمن وثوابه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r7.claim: The paired attributes suit that faith and disbelief include belief and speech; legal rulings of faith require the two testimonies, and disbelief also commonly involves speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p8/r7.anchor: لإشتمال الكفر والإيمان على الاعتقاد والقول أما إشتمال الإيمان على القول فظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.claim: The Muslims camped at the bank nearer Medina; al-dunyā is the feminine of al-adnā.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.anchor: {بالعدوة الدنيا} أي: بشفير الوادي الأدنى إلى المدينة، والدنيا. تأنيث الأدنى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.claim: The polytheist enemy camped at the bank farther from Medina; al-quṣwā is the feminine of al-aqṣā.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.anchor: {وهم} يعني عدوكم من المشركين، {بالعدوة القصوى} بشفير الوادي الأقصى من المدينة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Basrans read both occurrences with kasra on ʿayn; the others use ḍamma, two dialectal forms like kaswa and rashwa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل البصرة "بالعدوة" بكسر العين فيهما، والباقون بضمهما، وهما لغتان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.claim: The caravan is Abū Sufyān and his companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.anchor: يعني: العير يريد أبا سفيان وأصحابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.claim: The caravan was below the Muslims toward the seashore, three miles from Badr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.anchor: {أسفل منكم} أي: في موضع أسفل منكم إلى ساحل البحر، على ثلاثة أميال من بدر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.claim: The Muslims had set out for the caravan and the unbelievers to protect it, so they met without an appointment; had they arranged one, their small numbers and the enemy's size would have prevented agreement.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.anchor: خرجوا ليأخذوا العير وخرج الكفار ليمنعوها، فالتقوا على غير ميعاد، فقال تعالى: "ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r7.claim: God brought them together without an appointment to fulfill His decree: support His allies, strengthen His religion, and destroy His enemies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r7.anchor: {ولكن} الله جمعكم على غير ميعاد، {ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا} من نصر أوليائه وإعزاز دينه وإهلاك أعدائه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r8.claim: Those who die do so after seeing a clear sign and lesson and having proof established against them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r8.anchor: أي: ليموت من يموت على بينة رآها وعبرة عاينها وحجة قامت عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r9.claim: Those who live do so upon clear proof; the verse connects this to the rule that God does not punish until sending a messenger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r9.anchor: ويعيش من يعيش على بينة لوعده: "وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r10.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r10.claim: Ibn Isḥāq interprets perishing as disbelieving after proof is established and life as believing after such proof.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r10.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: معناه ليكفر من كفر بعد حجة قامت عليه، ويؤمن من آمن على مثل ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r11.claim: Qatāda interprets it as God letting those who go astray do so with proof and guiding those who are guided with proof.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: ليضل من ضل عن بينة، ويهدي من اهتدى على بينة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r12.claim: Readers in the Ḥijāz, Abū Bakr, and Yaʿqūb pronounce ḥayiya with two yāʾs; the others use one doubled yāʾ, matching the written form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p362#2/r12.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز وأبو بكر ويعقوب: "حيي" ببائين، مثل "خشي" وقرأ الآخرون: بياء واحدة مشددة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p363/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p363/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p363/r1.claim: God hears the believers' supplications and knows their intentions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r1.claim: The time clause is an appositive to 'the day of the Criterion' in 8:41.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r1.anchor: الدنيا } بدل من { يوم الفرقان } ، والعدوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r2.claim: The word for riverbank has three case-vowel forms; the common forms are ḍamma and kasra, with the latter read by Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r2.anchor: والعدوة بالحركات الثلاث شط الوادي وقد قرىء بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r3.claim: Al-quṣwā is the farther bank from Medina, the feminine of al-aqṣā; the expected form would change wāw to yāʾ, but the original form remains, like al-qawd, and is more common than al-quṣyā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r3.anchor: البعدى من المدينة، تأنيث الأقصى وكان قياسه قلب الواو ياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r4.claim: The caravan means either the trade caravan itself or its leaders.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r5.claim: This means in a lower place, namely the shore; it is an adverb functioning as predicate, and the clause is circumstantial to the preceding locative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r5.anchor: في مكان أسفل من مكانكم يعني الساحل، وهو منصوب على الظرف واقع موقع الخبر

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r6.claim: Mentioning the caravan displays the enemy's strength, support from the caravan, resolve to fight for it and hold their positions, against the Muslims' weakness and disorganization; the near bank was soft, difficult to cross, and had no water, unlike the far bank.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r6.anchor: وفائدتها الدلالة على قوة العدو واستظهارهم بالركب وحرصهم على المقاتلة عنها

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r7.claim: If both sides had arranged a battle after seeing the imbalance, the Muslims would have failed to keep the appointment from fear and despair; the outcome therefore revealed a miraculous divine victory and increased their faith and gratitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r7.anchor: لو تواعدتم أنتم وهم القتال ثم علمتم حالكم وحالهم لاختلفتم أنتم في الميعاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r8.claim: God brought them together without an appointment to fulfill His decree: aiding His allies and defeating His enemies.
