BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r8.anchor: حقيقا بأن يفعل وهو نصر أوليائه وقهر أعدائه

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r9.claim: The phrase may mean that some die and others live after witnessing clear proof, leaving no excuse, since Badr was a manifest sign; or that unbelief and faith emerge from clear proof, using death and life metaphorically for those states.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r9.anchor: ليموت من يموت عن بينة عاينها ويعيش من يعيش عن حجة شاهدها

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r10.claim: Those who perish or live may be approaching that fate, or may be people so described in God's knowledge and decree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r10.anchor: والمراد بمن هلك ومن حي المشارف للهلاك والحياة، أو من هذا حاله في علم الله وقضائه

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r11.claim: The verb is also read with fatḥa on yāʾ; Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr, and Yaʿqūb read ḥayya with the two yāʾs pronounced separately.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r11.anchor: وقرىء " ليهلك " بالفتح وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو بكر ويعقوب من " حيي " بفك الإدغام

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r12.claim: God hears the unbeliever's confession and knows his punishment, and hears the believer and knows his reward; the paired attributes suit speech and belief.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:42/r12.anchor: بكفر من كفر وعقابه، وإيمان من آمن وثوابه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r4.claim: Calling it the day the two groups met adds that the encounter was not planned by either side but arranged by God; merely saying ‘the day of Badr’ would omit this lesson.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r4.anchor: أي عن غير قصد من الفرقين بل بمخص تدبير الله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r5.claim: The nearer bank was closer to Medina; the farther bank lay farther from it, nearer the sea.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r5.anchor: بالعدوة الدنيا } اي القربى إلى المدينة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read al-ʿudwa with kasra; the other readers read it with damma.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r6.anchor: بالكسر في قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو ويعقوب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p219/r7.claim: The expected form would turn the waw into a ya, and that form occurs, but the form with waw is more common, as with istawsaba versus the rarer istasaba.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r1.claim: Al-ʿudwa is a bank or edge of a valley; its root-field turns on agitation and related ideas of adjacency, stillness, turning, return, and racing, suggesting raised ground beside a stream.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r1.anchor: فكأنها الموضع الذي علا عن محل فكان السيل موضعا للعدو

BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r2.claim: The caravan was the trading party the Muslims had hoped to intercept, led by Abu Sufyan; it lay below both armies toward the sea, about three miles away according to al-Baghawi.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r2.anchor: أي العير الذي فيه المتجر الذي خرجتم لاقتطاعه ورئيس جماعته أبو سفيان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r3.claim: The caravan’s location and the Quraysh army’s confident position show how much stronger the enemy appeared and how weak the Muslims were, making their victory a divine act.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r3.anchor: وإلى مثل هذه المعاني أشار تصوير مكانهم ومكان الركب إيماء إلى ما كان فيه العدو من قوة الشوكة وتكامل العدة وتمهد أسباب الغلبة وضعف حال المسلمين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r4.claim: When Salama ibn Salama ibn Waqsh disparaged the defeated Quraysh as bald old women, the Prophet replied that they were leaders whose sight would inspire fear and whose orders Salama would obey.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r4.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لسلمة بن سلامة بن وقش رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r5.claim: Against al-Baydawi, following al-Kashshaf, the near bank was not uniquely waterless and sinking sand: Muslims reached the water first, and rain compacted their ground while impeding the enemy.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p220/r5.anchor: وما في البيضاوي تبعا للكشاف من أن العدوة الدنيا كانت تسوخ فيها الأقدام ولا ماء بها تقدم زده أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r1.claim: A planned meeting would likely have failed because the camps were far apart and could not coordinate their pace, and because the Muslims feared the enemy; God could also have made Quraysh avoid the meeting, as at Badr al-Mawʿid.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r1.anchor: أحدهما بعد المسافة التي كنتم بها منها وتعذر توقيت سير كل فريق بسير صاحبه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r2.claim: Abu Jahl said that if the conflict were against people, Quraysh were strong enough, but if Muhammad’s claim that they fought God were true, nobody could withstand God; he also admitted to al-Akhnas that Muhammad never lied.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r2.anchor: قول أبي جهل الذي كان السبب الأعظم في اللقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r3.claim: Abu Jahl told al-Akhnas ibn Shariq that Muhammad was truthful and had never lied, even as God hardened the enemy’s hearts to bring about the encounter.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r3.anchor: وقوله أيضا في هذه الغزوة للأخنس بن شريق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r4.claim: God arranged the unplanned meeting: need drew the Muslims toward the caravan, they were promised one of two parties, Quraysh were compelled to defend it, and its escape left them arriving at Badr in pride and display.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r5.speaker: أبو جهل
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r5.claim: Abu Jahl vowed not to return until Quraysh sacrificed camels, drank wine, and entertained themselves at Badr so that the Arabs would fear them thereafter; this displays their pride before defeat.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r5.anchor: لا نرجع حتى نرد بدرا فننحر بها الجزور ونشرب الخمور وتعزف علينا القيان ونطعم من حضرنا من العرب فلا يزالون يهابوننا مدى الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r6.claim: God’s predetermined decree exalted His religion by honoring the Muslims and humiliating Quraysh, bringing about their killing and capture as destined.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r6.anchor: أي مقدرا في الأزل من لقائهم وما وقع فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r7.claim: The extraordinary outcome let each side perish or live on clear evidence: Badr proved the Messenger’s promises true and his opponents’ confident claims false despite appearances favoring them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r7.anchor: لما بان من صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الوقعة في كل ما وعد به وكذب الكفار في كل ما كانوا يقولونه قاطعين به مع أن ظاهر الحال يقضي لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r8.claim: Nafiʿ, al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr from Asim pronounce both yāʾs distinctly, signaling fullest life through Islam; the remaining readers assimilate them, signaling lesser life.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p221/r8.anchor: قراءة نافع والبزي عن ابن كثير وأبي بكر عن عاصم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r1.claim: The people who later say that their religion has deluded them reveal who was truly deceived; God hears their statements and knows their concealed thoughts, so they should fear Him and abandon their dispute.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r1.anchor: فيحنئذ تبين المغرور وكشفت عجائب المقدور

BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p222/r2.claim: God hears what they say and knows what they conceal; this should humble them and turn them from disputing out of fear.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the near side as the bank of the valley; Qatada is reported to give the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : اذ انتم بالعدوة الدنيا قال : شاطئ الوادي . وروى عن قتادة نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r2.claim: The Muslims were on the side of the valley nearest Medina.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق اذ انتم بالعدوة الدنيا الى المدينة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r3.claim: The far side was the farthest bank of the valley.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة وهم بالعدوة القصوى وهم بشفير الوادي الاقصى

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r4.claim: The far side of the valley was toward Mecca.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ثنا يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه وهم بالعدوة القصوى الوادي إلى مكة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس والركب اسفل منكم قال الركب : أو سفيان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r6.claim: The caravan meant Abu Sufyan and his party, positioned farther down toward the coast.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ثنا يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه والركب اسفل منكم يعني : أبا سفيان وغيره ، وهي اسفل من ذلك نحو الساحل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r7.speaker: هشام بن عروة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r7.claim: Abu Sufyan was down the valley with seventy riders, while Quraysh numbered 950; after he urged them from al-Juhfa to turn back, they insisted on reaching Badr's water.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r7.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة في قول الله : والركب اسفل منكم وكان أبو سفيان اسفل الوادي في سبعين راكبا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r8.claim: Had both sides arranged a meeting, learning the enemy's greater numbers and their own smaller numbers would have kept them from meeting.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1707#2/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : وحدثني يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r1.claim: God carried out by His power what He had willed: exalting Islam and its people and humbling disbelief and its people, without their arranging it, through His gracious care.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r1.anchor: وبه عن أبيه ولكن ليقضي الله امرا كان مفعولا اي ليقضي ما اراد بقدرته من اعزاز الاسلام واهله واذلال الكفر واهله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r2.claim: The Prophet's party set out seeking the caravan, while Quraysh left Mecca to defend it; God brought them together for battle to distinguish truth from falsehood, honor Islam, and humble polytheism.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق حدثني يحيى بن عباد بن الزبير عن ابيه ولكن ليقضي الله امرا كان مفعولا فاخرجه الله ومن معه الى العير

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r3.claim: The purpose was that disbelief follow clear proof, after people saw the signs, and that belief likewise follow such proof.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1708/r3.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق وحدثني يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r1.claim: Idh is an appositive to “the day the two armies met” and a temporal adverb for “We sent down,” locating the descent at their positions on the banks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r1.anchor: إذ } بدل من { يوم التقى الجمعان } ( الأنفال : 41 ) فهو ظرف ب { لأنزلنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r2.claim: The detailed setting recalls a perilous encounter with a well-equipped enemy and highlights God's great care; Quranic geography is recounted for its lesson, not as description alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r2.anchor: تنبيههم للطف عظيم حفهم من الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r3.claim: The noun is read with damma by the majority and with kasra by Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub; damma and kasra are the more eloquent forms among the three vowels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r3.anchor: فقرأه الجمهور بضم العين ، وقرأه ابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، و يعقوب بكسر العين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r4.claim: The banks are the two shores of the Badr valley, Badr being a water source: the nearer bank faced Medina, while the farther bank toward Mecca was a dune.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r4.anchor: وبدر اسم ماء . { والدنيا } هي القريبة أي العدوة التي من جهة المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r5.claim: The labels near and far do not rank the banks; Muslims had wanted the firmer far bank, so the enemy's arrival there initially dismayed them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r5.anchor: لأنها أصلب أرضا فليس للوصف بالدنو والقصو أثر في تفضيل إحدى العدوتين على الأخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r6.claim: Rain packed the Muslims' soft sandy ground so they could move, but made the ground occupied by Quraysh difficult, delaying their march and helping the Muslims reach Badr first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p15#2/r6.anchor: أرسل الله المطر وكان الوادي دهسا فلبد المطر الأرض ولم يعقهم عن المسير وأصاب الأرض التي بها قريش فعطلهم عن الرحيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r1.claim: The pronoun “they” refers to the other gathering, the Quraysh army, understood from the dual “two armies” after the verse addressed the Muslims as “you.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r1.anchor: وضمير { وهم } عائد إلى ما في لفظ { الجمعان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r2.claim: Al-rakb is the Quraysh caravan returning from Syria, also called al-ayr; its forty men were traveling on the lower coastal route, leaving Badr's water to their left.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r2.anchor: هو ركب قريش الراجعون من الشام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r3.claim: When Abu Sufyan learned the Muslims were pursuing his caravan, he turned it from the Badr road onto the coastal route to escape, where it traveled on lower plains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r3.anchor: ذلك أن أبا سفيان لما بلغه أن المسلمين خرجوا لتلقي عيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r4.claim: The Muslims lay between Abu Sufyan's force on the far bank and the caravan below them; if the enemy had noticed, it could have trapped them. They hoped to seize the caravan, as 8:7 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r4.anchor: والمعنى : والركب بالجهة السفلى منكم ، وهي جهة البحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r5.claim: Asfal is a locative adverb functioning as the predicate of al-rakb: the caravan had passed below them, although they hoped to catch and plunder it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r5.anchor: وانتصب { أسفل } على الظرفية المكانية وهو في محل رفع خبر عن ( الركب )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r6.claim: The apparent odds favored Quraysh: they had strength, water, and firmer ground, while Muslims faced soft sand and little water, and the caravan was safely behind the enemy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r6.anchor: فإنهم كانوا حينئذ في أشد ما يكون فيه جيش تجاه عدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r7.claim: God reversed the situation through rain, water, and the enemy's carelessness, granting victory where Muslims least expected it; recalling the scene prompts gratitude, trust in God's promise, and reliance on Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p16/r7.anchor: فكان من عجيب عناية الله بالمسلمين أن قلب تلك الحالة رأسا على عقب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r1.claim: The conditional clause is circumstantial to the two armies' meeting: they met without arrangement, at one time and in neighboring, facing locations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r1.anchor: وجملة { ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد } في موضع الحال من { الجمعان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r2.claim: Disagreement in the appointment means one side would be late for the agreed time, so both would not arrive together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r2.anchor: اختلاف وقته بأن يتأخر أحد الفريقين عن الوقت المحدود فلم يأتوا على سواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r3.claim: Some commentators supply that the Muslims would have realized their small numbers against the enemy's large force; Ibn Ashur rejects this because it predicts failure to attend, not mismatched timing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r3.anchor: ومنهم من اضطر إلى تقدير كلام محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r4.claim: Another proposed that Muslims would learn their weakness and Quraysh would fear them, making one side hesitate; Ibn Ashur says this also implies nonattendance rather than differing appointment times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r4.anchor: ومنهم من قدر : وعلمتم قلتكم وشعر المشركون بالخوف منكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r5.claim: Some commentators explain the mismatch by ordinary interruptions and contingencies; Ibn Ashur calls this the closest proposal but still not fully satisfying.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r5.anchor: ومنهم من جعل ذلك لما لا يخلو عنه الناس من عروض العوارض والقواطع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur reads this as “the Suhaybiyya لو”: the answer remains true whether the condition is imagined or not, either because it is likelier without the condition or regardless of it; he cross-refers to 8:23 and 6:111.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r6.anchor: فالوجه في تفسير هذه الآية أن { لو } هذه من قبيل ( لو ) الصهيبية فإن لها استعمالات ملاكها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r7.speaker: طفيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r7.claim: Tufayl's praise poem says even a mother enduring the same hardship would not tire, illustrating the construction's point that the result holds all the more in ordinary cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p18/r7.anchor: ومن هذا قول طفيل في الثناء على بني جعفر بن كلاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r1.claim: The sense is that a planned meeting would probably have had unequal arrival times, since appointments then used approximate parts of the day; arriving together without a plan shows God's facilitation and promised victory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r1.anchor: لأن التوقيت كان في تلك الأزمان تقريبا يقدرونه بأجزاء النهار كالضحى والعصر والغروب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r2.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r2.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'far's elegy uses “as if they had an appointment” for sequential events, a different comparison from the verse's hypothetical about missing the same meeting time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r2.anchor: كما قال الأسود بن يعفر يرثي هلاك أحلافه وأنصاره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r3.claim: The plural “you would differ” includes both armies, with the addressees grammatically given precedence over the absent group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r3.anchor: وضمير { اختلفتم } على الوجوه كلها شامل للفريقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r4.claim: The adversative means they did not arrange the meeting but arrived together so God could bring about His intended victory over the polytheists; their coincidence was divinely determined.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r4.anchor: ولكن لم تتواعدوا وجئتم على غير اتعاد ليقضي الله أي ليحقق وينجز ما أراده من نصركم على المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r5.claim: Amr here means a great, important affair rather than an ordinary command; its indefinite form magnifies it, and the sense links to 19:21 and 33:38.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r5.anchor: ومعنى { أمرا } هنا الشيء العظيم ، فتنكيره للتعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur points to his earlier discussion of “if He had made them hear” in this sura and his treatment of the related construction in al-An'am.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p19/r6.anchor: وقد تقدمت الإشارة إلى هذا عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r1.claim: Kana can mark a quality as established from the past, as in 30:47; here “was accomplished” means it was fixed in God's knowledge as certain to occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r1.anchor: و { كان } تدل على تحقق ثبوت معنى خبرها لاسمها من الماضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r2.claim: The event is described with a passive participle as if already done: God would enact a great event destined since eternity to occur despite ordinary impediments.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r2.anchor: لينجز الله ويوقع حدثا عظيما متصفا منذ القدم بأنه محقق الوقوع عند إبانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r3.claim: The clause is an explicative appositive to God's bringing about the affair: Muslim victory and defeat of the polytheists entail the perishing of the defeated and revival of the victorious, with clear evidence before both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r3.anchor: وجملة : { ليهلك من هلك عن بينة } في موضع بدل الاشتمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r4.claim: The second purpose lam reinforces the first; without it, yahlik would be nominative rather than subjunctive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r4.anchor: ودخول لام التعليل على فعل { يهلك } تأكيد للام الداخلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r5.claim: Perishing and life figuratively mean loss of strength and a community's rise; their contrast is like 9:42, 36:70, and 6:122, since Muslims were few and Quraysh powerful before Badr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r5.anchor: والهلاك والحياة مستعاران لمعنى ذهاب الشوكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r6.claim: Badr's outcome visibly demonstrated God's support for one people and abandonment of another, leaving no doubt and no excuse for the defeated while obliging the survivors to give thanks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p20/r6.anchor: أي عن حجة ظاهرة تدل على تأييد الله قوما وخذله آخرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r1.claim: The words are figurative rather than literal: literal death could suit yahlik, but not yahya, since the survivors were already alive before Badr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r1.anchor: ومن البعيد حمل { يهلك } و { يحيى } على الحقيقة لأنه وإن تحمله المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r2.claim: The figurative sense of عن is “after”: destruction and life emerge from, and are manifest through, a clear proof clarifying their causes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r2.anchor: ودل معنى المجاوزة الذي في { عن } على أن المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r3.claim: Nafi, al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr from Asim, Yaqub, and Khalaf articulate both y sounds in حيي; the remaining readers assimilate one into the other. Both are eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، والبزي عن ابن كثير ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r4.claim: The closing description means God heard the Muslims' prayer, discussions about going to Badr, and wish for the unarmed caravan; He also knows their unspoken thoughts and what serves their future glory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p22/r4.anchor: تذييل يشير إلى أن الله سميع دعاء المسلمين طلب النصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r1.claim: The governing word for idh is iltaqā, met, in the preceding context.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r2.claim: Al-ʿidwa is the edge of the valley, a difficult bank that prevents what lies in the valley from crossing; the term relates to ʿadā, going beyond or preventing passage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r2.anchor: وبالعدوة شفير الوادي وحرفه الذي يتعذر المشي فيه بمنزلة رحا البير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r3.claim: The cited poem's ʿadatanī attests the sense of being turned aside or prevented from visiting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r3.anchor: عدتني عن زيارتك العوادي ... وحالت دونها حرب زبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r4.claim: The bank or open space alongside the valley is called ʿidwa by proximity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r4.anchor: وتسمى الضفة والفضاء المساير للوادي عدوة للمجاورة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r5.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r5.claim: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the word with ḍamma; Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr use kasra, two dialects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «بالعدوة» بضم العين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r6.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وعمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, and ʿAmr read it with fatḥa; it may be a verbal noun, while Abu al-Fath calls it a third dialect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وعمرو «بالعدوة» بفتح العين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud's codex has ʿulyā and suflā instead of dunyā and quṣwā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r7.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود «إذ أنتم بالعدوة العليا وهم بالعدوة السفلى» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r8.claim: The names are relative to Medina; Badr's valley runs east from the battle site, and Medina is east of it by two stages, as the author's father had seen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r8.anchor: وقوله الدنيا والقصوى إنما بالإضافة إلى المدينة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Badr is between Mecca and Medina.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بدر بين مكة والمدينة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r10.claim: Dunyā derives from nearness and quṣwā from distance; quṣwā is anomalous where the expected form would use yāʾ, as al-Khalil explains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r10.anchor: والدنيا من الدنو، والقصوى من القصو، وهو البعد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r11.claim: The commentators identify the caravan as Abu Sufyan's group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r11.anchor: والركب بإجماع من المفسرين غير أبي سفيان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r12.claim: Rakb is a collective noun specifically for camel riders; it can take a plural like ṣāḥib/ṣuḥb or tājir/tujjar but is not used for very large groups.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p532#2/r12.anchor: ولا يقال ركب إلا لركاب الإبل وهو من أسماء الجمع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r1.speaker: القتبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r1.claim: Al-Qutaybi says rakb means about ten people, but Ibn ʿAtiyya rejects this because the Prophet called even three people a rakb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r1.anchor: وقال القتبي: الركب العشرة ونحوها، وهذا غير جيد لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r2.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r2.claim: Sibawayh parses asfal as genitive by an implied phrase meaning in a lower place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r2.anchor: وقوله أسفل في موضع خفض تقديره في مكان أسفل كذا قال سيبويه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r3.claim: Abu Hatim parses asfal as an adverbial accusative; alternatively the phrase means the caravan's place was below or it was situated below.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: نصب «أسفل» على الظرف ويجوز «الركب أسفل» على معنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r4.claim: Abu Sufyan had turned away from Badr after hearing of the Prophet and taken the coastal route, so his caravan was below the upper valley from its direction of approach.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r4.anchor: وكان الركب ومدبر أمره أبو سفيان بن حرب قد نكب عن بدر حين نذر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r5.claim: Mujahid says the Syrian trading party and the Muslims and Quraysh were unaware of one another until they met at Badr's water, fought, and the Muslims captured them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد في كتاب الطبري: أقبل أبو سفيان وأصحابه من الشام تجارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya objects that indications of awareness among the groups emerge from the full account of the battle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وفي هذا تعقب، وكان من هذه الفرق شعور يبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r7.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r7.claim: Al-Tabari and others say that if they had arranged to meet and then seen their numbers, they would have failed to meet.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r8.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawi attributes failure to meet to obstacles and interruptions; Ibn ʿAtiyya rejects this as an unsound reading and prefers the verse's point about God's enabling the encounter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r8.anchor:
وقال المهدوي: المعنى أي لاختلفتم بالقواطع والعوارض القاطعة بين الناس.
قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا نيل واضح،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r9.claim: The point is God's favor and power at Badr: even if they had planned and exerted themselves, the encounter could not have happened this way without God's facilitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r9.anchor: أن المقصد من الآية نعمة الله وقدرته في قصة بدر وتيسيره ما يسر من ذلك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r10.claim: God brought to pass and manifested a matter decreed from the beginning for them at its appointed time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r10.anchor: لينفذ ويظهر أمرا قد قدره في الأول مفعولا لكم بشرط وجودكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r11.claim: Al-Tabari takes death and life literally: those killed among unbelievers died after divine clarification and the message removed their excuse; those who lived had the same clear proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r11.anchor: قال الطبري: المعنى ليقتل من قتل من كفار قريش وغيرهم ببيان من الله وإعذار بالرسالة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r12.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r12.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others take perishing as disbelief and life as faith, metaphorically: Badr became a clear sign by which people believed or disbelieved.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r12.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق وغيره: معنى ليهلك أي ليكفر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r13.speaker: الأعمش وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r13.claim: Most readers pronounce the second lām of liyahlika with kasra; al-Aʿmash reads fatḥa, also transmitted by ʿIsma from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r13.anchor: وقرأ الناس «ليهلك» بكسر اللام الثانية وقرأ الأعمش «ليهلك» بفتح اللام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r14.claim: Bayyina is an adjective meaning a clear case or proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r14.anchor: و «البينة» صفة أي عن قضية بينة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r15.claim: The first lām in liyahlika answers to the lām in liyaqḍiya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533/r15.anchor: واللام الأولى في قوله ليهلك رد على اللام في قوله ليقضي.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير عن قنبل وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم عن حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r1.claim: Qunbul's Ibn Kathir transmission, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read ḥayya with one yāʾ and shadda.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في رواية قنبل وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص «من حي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير عن البزي وعاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r2.claim: Nafiʿ, al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim pronounce both yāʾs, the first with kasra and second with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير في رواية البزي وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر «من حيي» بإظهار الياءين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r3.claim: The one-yāʾ reading resembles sound roots such as ʿaḍḍa and shamma because the yāʾ has a fixed vowel; the behavior of jawārī illustrates this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r3.anchor: قال من قرأ «حي» فلأن الياء قد لزمتها الحركة فصار الفعل بلزوم الحركة لها مشبها بالصحيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r4.claim: The cited poet's ʿayū bi-amrihim is an example of the assimilated pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r4.anchor: وعلى نحو «حي» جاء قول الشاعر: [مجزوء الكامل] عيوا بأمرهم كما ...

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r5.claim: Labid's ʿayya dhū al-lubb is another poetic example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r5.anchor: ومنه قول لبيد: [الرمل] سألتني جارتي عن أمتي ... وإذا ما عي ذو اللب سأل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r6.claim: Al-Mutalammis's ḥayya dhubābuhu, also transmitted as janna dhubābuhu, attests the form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r6.anchor: وقول المتلمس: [الطويل] فهذا أوان العرض حي ذبابه ... زنابيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli and others allow past-tense assimilation when the yāʾ has a fixed vowel in the imperfect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي وغيره: هذا أن كل موضع تلزم الحركة فيه ياء مستقبلية فالإدغام في ماضيه جائز،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r8.claim: The yuḥyī form in Q 46:33 and Q 75:40 is not assimilated because its fatḥa is not fixed and disappears in indicative or jussive forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r8.anchor: ألا ترى أن قوله تعالى: على أن يحيي الموتى [الأحقاف: 33، القيامة: 40] لا يجوز الإدغام فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r9.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects an anonymous poem offered for this form as an unknown verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r9.anchor: ولا يلتفت إلى ما أنشد بعضهم لأنه بيت مجهول: [الكامل]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r10.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r10.claim: For the two-yāʾ reading, Sibawayh says Yunus reported hearing Arabs use the language, including aḥyāʾā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r10.anchor: فإن سيبويه قال: أخبرنا بهذه اللغة يونس،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r11.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r11.claim: Abu Hatim accepts both distinct and assimilated forms as common Arabic, advises reading what one learned, and notes the spelling has one yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: القراءة إظهار الياءين والإدغام حسن فاقرأ كيف تعلمت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Abu ʿAli has comprehensively treated the forms derived from ḥayiya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p533#2/r12.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وفي هذه اللفظة استوعب أبو علي القول فيما تصرف من «حيي»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read العدوة with kasra on the ʿayn in both occurrences.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالعدوة والعدوة العين فيهما مكسورة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read both instances with ḍamma on ʿayn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بضم العين فيهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r3.speaker: الأخفش وثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash says only the kasra form is attested from Arabs, while Thaʿlab says ḍamma is the more common of the two dialect forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش لم يسمع من العرب إلا الكسر وقال ثعلب بل الضم أكثر اللغتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r4.speaker: ابن السكيت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt says ʿudwa means the side of a valley, with two reported plural forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r4.anchor: قال ابن السكيت عدوة الوادي وعدوته جانبه والجمع عدى وعدى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r5.claim: Dunyā and quṣwā are feminine forms of adnā and aqṣā. Arabs usually change wāw to yāʾ in this pattern after an initial ḍamma, as in الدنيا and العليا, but the Hijaz retains wāw in القصوى unusually; others say القصيا.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r5.anchor: الدنيا تأنيث الأدنى وضدها القصوى وهي تأنيث الأقصى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r6.claim: The Muslims were at the nearer bank of the valley toward Medina and their enemy at the farther bank toward Mecca; the two forces camped in this arrangement at Badr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون إذ أنتم بشفير الوادي الأدنى من المدينة وعدوكم بشفيره الأقصى من مكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r7.claim: The caravan was Abū Sufyān and his companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r7.anchor: والركب أبو سفيان وأصحابه قال الزجاج من نصب أسفل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r8.claim: Qatāda says the Muslims were on the upper part of the valley and the polytheists below.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r8.anchor: قال قتادة وكان المسلمون أعلى الوادي والمشركون أسفله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the accusative أسفل means the caravan was at a lower place than you; it may be nominative if read according to the sense that the caravan was farther below.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج من نصب أسفل اراد والركب مكانا أسفل منكم ويجوز الرفع على المعنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r10.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r10.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says that had they arranged a meeting and then learned the enemy’s numbers, they would have postponed it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r10.anchor: لو تواعدتم ثم بلغكم كثرتهم لتأخرتم عن الميعاد قاله ابن اسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r11.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r11.claim: Abū Sulaymān says a planned meeting at the place where they met on the two banks of Badr would have failed to coincide.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r11.anchor: لو تواعدتم على الاجتماع في المكان الذي اجتمعتم فيه من عدوتي وادي بدر لاختلفتم في الميعاد قاله أبو سليمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r12.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r12.claim: Al-Māwardī says the divergence could have been an unintended increase or decrease, or an advance or delay.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p361/r12.anchor: قال الماوردي كانت تقع الزيادة والنقصان أو التقدم والتأخر من غير قصد لذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r1.claim: The matter God decreed was Islam’s elevation and the humiliation of polytheism.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r2.speaker: خلف عن يحيى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r2.claim: Khalaf reports from Yaḥyā the reading ليهلك with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r2.anchor: وروى خلف عن يحيى ليهلك بضم الياء وفتح اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وقنبل عن ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r3.claim: These readers pronounce حي with one doubled yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي من حي بياء واحدة مشددة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r4.speaker: شبل عن ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r4.claim: Shibl from Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim report two yāʾs, as does Nāfiʿ; one yāʾ is not assimilated, while the other reading assimilates the two identical letters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r4.anchor: وروى شبل عن ابن كثير وابو بكر عن عاصم حيي بياءين الأولى مكسورة والثانية مفتوحة وهي قراءة نافع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r5.claim: One interpretation is that those killed among the polytheists were killed on clear proof and their survivors remained on clear proof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r5.anchor: ليقتل من قتل من المشركين عن حجة ويبقى من بقي منهم عن حجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r6.claim: A second interpretation is that whoever disbelieves does so after clear proof, and whoever believes does so after clear proof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p362/r6.anchor: ليكفر من كفر بعد حجة ويؤمن من آمن عن حجة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r1.claim: The Muslims camped on the nearer side of the valley toward Medina, while the polytheists camped on the farther side toward Mecca.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r1.anchor: أي: إذ أنتم نزول بعدوة الوادي الدنيا القريبة إلى المدينة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r2.claim: The caravan below the Muslims was Abu Sufyan’s trade caravan, positioned toward the seashore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r2.anchor: العير الذي فيه أبو سفيان بما معه من التجارة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r3.claim: Had the two sides arranged a meeting, they would have missed it because the circumstances made the encounter unlikely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r3.anchor: {ولو تواعدتم} أي: أنتم والمشركون إلى مكان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr that, if the meeting had been planned, the Muslims would have turned away on learning the enemy’s numbers and their own smaller force.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: وحدثني يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير، عن أبيه في هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r5.claim: God brought about what He willed through His power: strengthening Islam and its people and humbling polytheism and its people, without the Muslims arranging it, by His subtle providence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r5.anchor: ليقضي الله ما أراد بقدرته من إعزاز الإسلام وأهله، وإذلال الشرك وأهله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r6.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik says the Prophet and Muslims set out seeking Quraysh’s caravan, but God brought them face to face with their enemy without an appointment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r6.anchor: وفي حديث كعب بن مالك قال: إنما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمون يريدون عير قريش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r7.speaker: عمير بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r7.claim: Umayr ibn Ishaq reports that Abu Sufyan’s Syrian caravan and Abu Jahl’s force to protect it reached Badr unaware of one another, until water carriers met and the troops advanced.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r7.anchor: عن ابن عون، عن عمير بن إسحاق قال: أقبل أبو سفيان في الركب من الشام، وخرج أبو جهل ليمنعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts how scouts Basbas and Adi learned the caravan’s arrival; Abu Sufyan found Yathrib date pits in their camels’ droppings, hurried the caravan along the coast, and told Quraysh to return.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p66/r8.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق في السيرة: ومضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Abu Jahl refusing to return after the caravan was saved, insisting Quraysh camp at Badr for three days of feasting and display so Arabs would fear them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r1.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: والله (4) لا نرجع حتى نأتي بدرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r2.speaker: الأخنس بن شريق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r2.claim: Al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq persuaded Banu Zuhrah that God had saved their property and leader, so they returned; Banu Adi also did not attend Badr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r2.anchor: فقال الأخنس بن شريق: يا معشر بني زهرة، إن الله قد نجى أموالكم، ونجى صاحبكم، فارجعوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet’s scouts captured Quraysh water carriers; after the Prophet rebuked the companions for beating truthful witnesses and releasing liars, he learned the enemy numbered about 900–1,000 and heard its leading names.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r3.anchor: إذا صدقاكم ضربتموهما، وإذا كذباكم تركتموهما. صدقا، والله إنهما لقريش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r4.claim: After hearing the captives’ account of Quraysh’s prominent leaders, the Prophet told the Muslims that Mecca had cast its choicest people before them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p67/r4.anchor: فأقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الناس فقال: "هذه مكة قد ألقت إليكم أفلاذ كبدها"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r1.speaker: سعد بن معاذ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r1.claim: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh proposed a shelter and mounts for the Prophet at Badr, with a route to join their supporters if defeated; he said absent Muslims loved and would support the Prophet had they known of the battle. The Prophet praised and prayed for him, and the shelter was built for the Prophet and Abu Bakr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r1.anchor: أن سعد بن معاذ قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، لما التقى الناس يوم بدر: يا رسول الله، ألا نبني لك عريشا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r2.claim: As Quraysh approached Badr at dawn, the Prophet prayed for their defeat, describing them as boastful, arrogant, and opposing God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68/r2.anchor: قال: "اللهم هذه (6) قريش قد أقبلت بفخرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that the event lets disbelief persist after proof and signs, and lets belief arise on their evidence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: أي ليكفر من كفر بعد الحجة، لما رأى من الآية والعبرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir endorses Ibn Ishaq’s explanation: God joined the forces unexpectedly to make truth prevail and its proof decisive, leaving no excuse; the disbeliever persists knowingly in falsehood, while the believer accepts guidance with insight. Faith gives hearts life.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir cites Aisha’s account of the slander episode: “those who perished” refers to those who spoke falsehood, slander, and calumny about her.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.anchor: وقالت عائشة في قصة الإفك: في هلك من هلك أي: قال فيها ما قال من الكذب والبهتان والإفك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p69/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p69/r1.claim: God hears the Muslims’ prayers, supplications, and cries for help, and knows that they deserve victory over their stubborn, hostile disbelieving enemies.

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r1.claim: These readers use kasra on ʿayn in both instances of العدوة; the other readers use ḍamma, and both are dialects.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: (بالعدوة) بكسر العين في الحرفين

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم والبزي عن ابن كثير وبصير عن الكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the two yāʾs distinctly in ويحيا.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r2.anchor: ويعقوب ويحيا من حيي بإظهار الياءين

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير وابن فليح وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r3.claim: These readers assimilate the two yāʾs into a doubled yāʾ; the second has a fixed vowel and the written form has one yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير في رواية القراءتين، وابن فليح وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي بياء مشددة على الإدغام

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r4.claim: Distinct pronunciation follows the related imperfect يحيى; Basrans reject assimilation in حيا يحيا since even a sound doubled verb favors clarity when its second radical is quiescent, and some Kufans allow assimilation.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r4.anchor: فأما الإظهار فلامتناع الإدغام في مضارعه من يحيا

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r5.claim: Al-ʿidwa is a side of a valley; its two sides are its edges and boundaries.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r5.anchor: العدوة: جانب الوادي، والجميع عداء وللوادي عدوتان

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r6.claim: Al-quṣwā is the feminine of al-aqṣā, like al-kubrā and al-ṣughrā.

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r7.claim: Here الدنيا means nearer toward Mecca; the word also means the first life and derives from wāw, changed to yāʾ for ease.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r7.anchor: والدنيا تأنيث الأدنى، يعني أدنى إلى جهة مكة

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r8.claim: قصي denotes distance: القصوى is farthest, أقصيته means moved away, and قصوت من القوم means kept apart.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r8.anchor: والقصي: البعد، وهو بالمكان الأقصى: الأبعد

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r9.claim: Rukb is a collective plural of rider, equivalent to rukbān; it describes people on camels, and related forms denote a rideable she-camel or a colt fit to ride.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r9.anchor: والركب: جمع راكب، كشارب وشرب، ركب يركب ركوبا

JISHUMI:v4p2943/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r10.claim: Sufl means lower, the opposite of high, with related forms سفل and تسفل.
JISHUMI:v4p2943/r10.anchor: والسفل: خلاف العلو، سفل يسفل سفالا وتسفل تسفلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.claim: ‘When’ is in apposition to ‘the Day of the Criterion,’ referring to Badr.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.claim: Al-ʿidwa means the bank or side of a valley; the word allows kasra, ḍamma, or fatḥa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.anchor: والعدوة : شط الوادي بالكسر والضم والفتح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.claim: A reading has ‘bihinna’ and another ‘al-ʿadiya,’ turning wāw into yāʾ because the barrier between it and kasra is weak.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( بهن وبالعدية ) على قلب الواو ياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.claim: Al-dunyā and al-quṣwā are feminine forms of al-adnā and al-aqṣā; the expected wāw-to-yāʾ change appears in al-dunyā, while al-quṣwā preserves root wāw, though al-quṣyā also occurs and al-quṣwā is more common.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.anchor: والدنيا والقصوى : تأنيث الأدنى والأقصى . فإن قلت : كلتاهما ( فعلى ) من بنات الواو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r5.claim: The near bank lies toward Medina and the far bank toward Mecca.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r5.anchor: والعدوة الدنيا مما يلي المدينة ، والقصوى مما يلي مكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r6.claim: The caravan consisted of forty men guiding the trade goods, positioned below the Muslims along the coast.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r6.anchor: يعني الركب الأربعين الذين كانوا يقودون العير أسفل منكم بالساحل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r7.claim: ‘Asfal’ is accusative as a locative adverb, meaning a place lower than theirs, though it has nominative syntactic status as the predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r7.anchor: وأسفل : نصب على الظرف ، معناه : مكانا أسفل من مكانكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r8.claim: The positions show the enemy’s stronger numbers, supplies, and tactical ground, while Muslim victory under those conditions demonstrates God’s power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r8.anchor: الفائدة فيه الإخبار عن الحال الدالة على قوة شأن العدو وشوكته ، وتكامل عدته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r9.claim: Quraysh had water and solid ground on their bank; the Muslims’ near bank was waterless, sandy, and difficult to walk across.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r9.anchor: أناخ بها المشركون كان فيها الماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r10.claim: The caravan behind Quraysh intensified their resolve to fight for their property; Arabs also took families and wealth to war to strengthen defense and prevent retreat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r10.anchor: وكانت العير وراء ظهور العدو مع كثرة عددهم ، فكانت الحماية دونها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r11.claim: The verse depicts God arranging Badr to establish His religion and exalt His word after promising the Muslims one of two parties without specifying which.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r11.anchor: وفيه تصوير ما دبر سبحانه من أمر وقعة بدر . ليقضي أمرا كان مفعولا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r12.claim: The Muslims set out hoping to capture the caravan, while Quraysh mobilized in fear after learning the Prophet had threatened their property; God arranged the forces’ positions and brought battle about.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r12.anchor: حتى خرجوا ليأخذوا العير راغبين في الخروج ، وشخص بقريش مرعوبين مما بلغهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r13.claim: Had the sides arranged a meeting, the Muslims’ small numbers and Quraysh’s fear of the Prophet and his followers would have prevented them from keeping the appointment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r13.anchor: لخالف بعضكم بعضا فثبطكم قلتكم وكثرتهم عن الوفاء بالموعد ، وثبطهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r14.claim: The purpose clause depends on an omitted phrase: God arranged matters to aid His friends and defeat His enemies; ‘that he perish’ is an appositional substitute.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r14.anchor: أمرا كان واجبا أن يفعل ، وهو نصر أوليائه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r15.claim: Perishing and living are metaphors for disbelief and Islam, so each person’s choice issues from clear proof rather than doubt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r15.anchor: واستعير الهلاك والحياة للكفر والإسلام ، أي ليصدر كفر من كفر عن وضوح بينة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r16.claim: Badr’s unmistakable signs left later unbelief as self-deception and obstinacy, while conversion should follow certainty that Islam is true.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r16.anchor: وذلك أن ما كان من وقعة بدر من الآيات الغر المحجلة التي من كفر بعدها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r17.claim: A reading has the lām in ‘li-yahlika’ with fatḥa; another articulates the doubled consonant in ‘ḥayya.’

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r18.claim: God knows how to arrange affairs and balance interests, and knows each group’s disbelief or faith and their punishment or reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p211#3/r18.anchor: أو لسميع عليم بكفر من كفر وعقابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r1.claim: The nearer bank is the edge of the valley at Badr toward Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r1.anchor: يعني شفير الوادي ببدر , الأدنى إلى المدينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r2.claim: The farther bank is the edge of the valley toward Mecca.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r2.anchor: يعني شفير الوادي الأقصى إلى مكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r3.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash defines the valley's ʿidwa as its lip or edge, above its bottom but below its top.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r3.anchor: عدوه الوادي هو ملطاط شفيره الذي هو أعلى من أسفله , وأسفل من أعلاه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r4.claim: The caravan below them was Abu Sufyan's caravan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r4.anchor: يعني عير أبي سفيان أسفل الوادي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi locates the caravan on the seashore, three miles away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي : على شاطىء البحر بثلاثة أميال

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r6.claim: One explanation says that even if they had arranged to meet, they would have differed unintentionally through delays, advances, additions, or omissions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r6.anchor: ولو تواعدتم أن تتفقوا مجتمعين لاختلفتم في الميعاد , بالتقديم والتأخير والزيادة والنقصان من غير قصد لذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq says they would have broken the appointment and retreated if they learned how numerous the enemy was compared with them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r7.anchor: ولو تواعدتم ثم بلغكم كثرة عدوكم مع قلة عددكم لتأخرتم فنقضتم الميعاد , قاله ابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r8.claim: A third explanation says that without God's help, obstacles and hindrances would have made them miss the appointment after hearing the enemy's strength.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r8.anchor: ولو تواعدتم ثم بلغكم كثرة عدوكم من غير معونة الله لكم لأخلفتم بالقواطع والعوائق في الميعاد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r9.claim: One view says the Quraysh killed at Badr died upon proof, while survivors remained alive through God's power.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r9.anchor: أحدهما : ليقتل ببدر من قتل من مشركي قريش عن حجة , وليبقى من بقي عن قدرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r10.claim: A second view says disbelievers among Quraysh disbelieved after proof of the promised outcome, while believers accepted the truth of their faith with knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p321/r10.anchor: ويؤمن من آمن بعد العلم بصحة إيمانهم

MUJAHID:v1p263#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p263#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p263#2/r1.claim: The caravan was Abu Sufyan and his merchants returning from Syria; unaware of each other, they met the Muslims' and Quraysh's water parties at Badr, fought, and the Muslims defeated and captured them.
MUJAHID:v1p263#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ والركب أسفل منكم ﴾ يعني به أبا سفيان وأصحابه مقبلين من الشام تجارا

MUQATIL:8:41-44/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r5.claim: The believers were on the near bank toward Medina; the Meccan polytheists were on the far bank toward Mecca.
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r5.anchor: يعني من دون الوادي على شاطئ مما يلي المدينة

MUQATIL:8:41-44/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r6.claim: The caravan was forty riders on the seashore, returning from Syria to Mecca, including Abu Sufyan, Amr ibn al-As, Makhrama ibn Nawfal, and Amr ibn Hisham.
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r6.anchor: على ساحل البحر أصحاب العير أربعين راكبا أقبلوا من الشام إلى مكة

MUQATIL:8:41-44/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r7.claim: Had believers and polytheists arranged a meeting, they would have failed to keep its time; God instead brought them together without an appointment.
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r7.anchor: ولو تواعدتم } أنتم والمشركون، { لاختلفتم في الميعاد

MUQATIL:8:41-44/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r8.claim: God brought about an inevitable matter, exalting Islam and its adherents while humiliating idolatry and its adherents.
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r8.anchor: ليعز الإسلام وأهله، ويذل الشرك وأهله

MUQATIL:8:41-44/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:41-44/r9.claim: The outcome lets one perish in disbelief or live by faith, each on the basis of clear proof.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r1.claim: Idh antum is either an appositive to the day of the Criterion or governed by an understood remember.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r1.anchor: إذ أنتم بدل من يوم الفرقان أو التقدير اذكروا إذ أنتم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r2.claim: Al-ʿudwa means the side or bank of a valley.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r2.anchor: ﴿ بالعدوة ﴾ شط الوادى وبالكسر فيهما مكى وبو عرمو

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r3.speaker: مكى وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r3.claim: Meccan readers and Abū ʿAmr read the word with kasra in both occurrences.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r3.anchor: وبالكسر فيهما مكى وبو عرمو ﴿ الدنيا ﴾ القربى إلى جهة الميدنة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r4.claim: Al-dunyā is the nearer bank toward Medina and al-quṣwā the farther one; they are feminine forms of adnā and aqṣā, with quṣwā retaining the original wāw.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r4.anchor: ﴿ الدنيا ﴾ القربى إلى جهة الميدنة تأنيث الأذنى ﴿ وهم بالعدوة القصوى ﴾ البعد عن المدينة تأنيث الأقصى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r5.claim: Al-rakb is the caravan, a collective in meaning for riders, positioned lower in the valley.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r5.anchor: ﴿ والركب ﴾ أى العير وهو جمع راكب فى المعنى أسلف منكم نصب على الظرف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r6.claim: Asfala is an adverbial accusative locating the caravan below the Muslims, about three miles down the valley; its syntactic position is a predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r6.anchor: مكانا أسفل من مكانكم يعنى فى أسفل الوادى بثلاثة أميال وهو مرفوع المحل لأنه خبر المبتدا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r7.claim: Had Muslims and Meccans arranged a battle date, they would have failed to keep it: fear of the opposing numbers and of the Prophet and Muslims would have deterred them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r7.anchor: ﴿ ولو تواعدتم ﴾ أنتم و أهل مكة وتواضعتم بينكم على موعد تلقتون فيه لبقتال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r8.claim: God brought the two sides together without an appointment to exalt Islam, raise its word, help His allies, and defeat His enemies.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r8.anchor: ولكن جمع بينكم بلا يمعاد ﴿ ليقضى الله أمرا كان مفعولا ﴾ من اعزاز دينه واعلاء كلمته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r9.claim: The purpose clause may attach to an omitted verb or directly to yaqḍiya.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r9.anchor: واللام تتعلق بمحذوف أى ليقضى الله أمرا كان ينبغى أن يفعل وهو نصر تاوليائه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r10.speaker: أبو منصور
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r10.claim: Abū Manṣūr says qaḍāʾ may mean judging what God already knew would occur, or completing what He intended; what He wills must happen.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو منصور رحمه الله القضاء يحتمل الحكم أى ليحكم ما قد علم أنه يكون كائنا أو ليتم أمرا كان قد أراده

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r11.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr assimilate the two matching consonants in ḥayya; the alternative preserves them because the second vowel is not fixed, though assimilation is more common.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r11.anchor: حيى نافع و أبو عمرو فالادغام لالتقاء المثلين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r12.claim: Death and life stand for disbelief and Islam: each should arise from clear proof, not doubt, and Badr was such a clear sign that later rejection was obstinacy while acceptance showed certainty.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p66/r12.anchor: استيعر الهلاك والحياة للكفر و الإسلام أى ليصدر كفر من كفر عن وضوح بينة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r1.claim: The visible positions of the two armies and the caravan show that victory comes from God, not numerical strength or material means.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r1.anchor: ليعلم الخلق أن النصر والغلبة لا تكون بالكثرة والأسباب بل بالله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r2.claim: The polytheists held the better, watered far bank; the Muslims were on soft, waterless ground where feet sank, while the caravan was behind the enemy despite their greater numbers and equipment.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r2.anchor: وكان العير وراء ظهور العدو مع كثرة عددهم وعدتعهم وقلة المسليمن وضعفهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r3.claim: God hears their words and knows the unbeliever's disbelief and punishment and the believer's faith and reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p67/r3.anchor: بكفر من كفر وعقابه وبايمان من آمن وثوابه

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r1.claim: The opening means either when God arranged matters this way or recall when you were there; al-ʿudwah is a valley bank.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى } أي أنزلنا إذ أنتم على هذه الصفة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r2.claim: The noun is read with ḍamma or kasra on ʿayn; both forms pluralize as عدى.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r2.anchor: وقرىء بضم العين وكسرها فعلى الضم يكون الجمع عدى، وعلى الكسر عدى

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r3.claim: Dunyā and quṣwā are feminine forms; quṣyā is also used, while Hijazi usage keeps the original wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r3.anchor: والدنيا: تأنيث الأدنى. والقصوى: تأنيث الأقصى. من دنا يدنو، وقصا يقصو. ويقال: القصيا. والأصل الواو، وهي لغة أهل الحجاز قصوى.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r4.claim: The near bank was toward Medina and the far bank toward Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r4.anchor: فالدنيا كانت مما يلي المدينة، والقصوى مما يلي مكة. أي إذ أنتم نزول بشفير الوادي بالجانب الأدنى إلى المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r5.claim: The caravan means Abu Sufyan and his company, with their goods below the Muslims near the coast.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r5.anchor: يعني ركب أبي سفيان وغيره. كانوا في موضع أسفل منهم إلى ساحل البحر فيه الأمتعة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r6.claim: Another view takes al-rakb as the camels carrying their goods, providentially kept safe as a favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي الإبل التي كانت تحمل أمتعتهم، وكانت في موضع يأمنون عليها توفيقا من الله عز وجل لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r7.claim: Al-rakb is the subject; asfal is a locative predicate meaning in a lower place.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r7.anchor: «الركب» ابتداء «أسفل منكم» ظرف في موضع الخبر. أي مكانا أسفل منكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r8.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r8.claim: They allow asfal as a comparative, meaning farther below you.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r8.anchor: وأجاز الأخفش والكسائي والفراء «الركب أسفل منكم» أي أشد تسفلا منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r9.speaker: ابن السكيت وابن فارس
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r9.claim: Most lexicographers reserve rakb and its forms for camel riders, not riders of horses or other mounts.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r9.anchor: وحكى ابن السكيت وأكثر أهل اللغة أنه لا يقال راكب وركب إلا للذي على الإبل

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r10.claim: A planned meeting would have failed because the enemy outnumbered the Muslims; knowing the disparity, the Muslims would have delayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r10.anchor: أي لم يكن يقع الاتفاق لكثرتهم وقلتكم فإنكم لو عرفتم كثرتهم لتأخرتم فوفق الله عز وجل لكم

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r11.claim: The destined matter is victory for believers and establishment of religion.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r12.claim: The lām depends on an omitted verb: God gathered them to decree the matter; the next lām repeats the gathering purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r12.anchor: واللام في «ليقضي» متعلقة بمحذوف. والمعنى: جمعهم ليقضي الله، ثم كررها فقال: { ليهلك }

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r13.claim: من is nominative and يحيى accusative, coordinated with ليهلك.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r13.anchor: «من» في موضع رفع. «ويحيا» في موضع نصب عطف على ليهلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r14.claim: Bayyinah is proof: destruction follows witnessed proof and a direct lesson, so the case is established; likewise life.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r14.anchor: والبينة إقامة الحجة والبرهان. أي ليموت من يموت عن بينة رآها وعبرة عاينها. فقامت عليه الحجة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r15.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r15.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes it as an unbeliever disbelieving after proof removes his excuse, and a believer believing on that basis.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r15.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: ليكفر من كفر بعد حجة قامت عليه وقطعت عذره، ويؤمن من آمن على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r16.speaker: أهل المدينة والبزي وأبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r16.claim: These readers preserve two yāʾs in من حيي; other readers use one doubled yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r16.anchor: وقرىء «من حيي» بيائين على الأصل. وبياء واحدة مشددة، الأولى قراءة أهل المدينة والبزي وأبي بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r17.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r17.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the doubled one-yāʾ reading because that is how it appears in the codex.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:42/r17.anchor: والثانية قراءة الباقين. وهي اختيار أبي عبيد لأنها كذلك وقعت في المصحف

QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r1.claim: The near bank is the city of knowledge and the seat of rational discrimination.
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r1.anchor: من مدينة العلم ومحل العقل الفرقاني

QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r2.claim: The far bank is the lower direction, remote from truth and the abode of knowledge; the caravan below is the natural faculties distinguished from psychic faculties.
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r2.anchor: الجهة السفلية البعيدة من الحق ومحل العلم وركب القوى الطبيعية الممتازة للقوى النفسانية

QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r3.claim: Had they arranged the encounter through reason and wisdom rather than spiritual discipline and unity, the timing would have differed because it was difficult and invited failure and cowardice.
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r3.anchor: اللقاء للمحاربة من طريق العقل والحكمة دون طريق الرياضة والوحدة

QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r4.claim: God acted to carry out a decree already ordained and certain to occur.
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r4.anchor: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا

QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r5.claim: One perishes on clear evidence because that evidence is embodied in a body destined to pass away; the truly living have evidence detached from the body and joined to the holy realm, source of enduring life.
QASHANI:8:41-42#2/r5.anchor: هي كونها مجردة عنه متصلة بعالم القدس الذي هو معدن الحياة الحقيقية الدائم البقاء

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r1.claim: The opening ‘when’ either depends on an omitted ‘remember’ or stands in apposition to ‘the Day of Criterion.’
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r1.anchor: في قوله : { إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا } قولان : أحدهما : أنه متعلق بمضمر معناه واذكروا

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and Abu ʿAmr read both occurrences with kasra; the others use damma. Both are dialect forms. Al-Akhfash knew only kasra, while Ahmad ibn Yahya says damma is more common; al-Kashshaf also reports fatha and al-ʿadiyya with waw changed to ya.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو { بالعدوة } بكسر العين في الحرفين .

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit defines ʿudwat al-wadi as the side of a valley, with plural forms ʿudan and ʿudiy.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : عدوة الوادي وعدوته جانبه ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r4.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says the kasra form is the Arabs’ speech and that he heard no other form.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش : الكسر كلام العرب لم يسمع عنهم غير ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r5.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says damma is the more common dialect form.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r5.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى : الضم في العدوة أكثر اللغتين

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
