RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports damma, fatha, and kasra, plus al-ʿadiyya formed by changing waw to ya across a weak barrier, as in al-fitya.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r6.anchor: وحكى صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الضم والفتح والكسر .

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r7.claim: Al-dunya is feminine of al-adna and al-quswa feminine of al-aqsa; qasā means distant. Though both are faʿla from waw, expected waw-to-ya appears in al-ʿulya, while al-quswa is anomalous and often preserves waw.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r7.anchor: وأما { الحيواة الدنيا } فتأنيث الأدنى وضده { القصوى } وهو تأنيث الأقصى

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r8.claim: The nearer bank is toward Medina and the farther bank toward Mecca; water lay with the polytheists, whose position was stronger, while the caravan was below the Muslims toward the seashore.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r8.anchor: المراد بالعدوة الدنيا ، ما يلي جانب المدينة ، وبالقصوى ، ما يلي جانب مكة وكان الماء في العدوة التي نزل بها المشركون

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r9.claim: Had the Muslims and Meccans arranged a battle, their small numbers against the Meccans’ larger force would have made them miss the appointed time.

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r10.claim: God established and supported the Muslims with victory so that an affair already destined and certain would be fulfilled.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r10.anchor: أي أنه يثبتكم الله ، وينصركم ، ليقضي أمرا كان مفعولا

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r11.claim: ‘So that whoever perished’ is grammatically an appositive replacing ‘so that God might fulfill.’
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r11.anchor: وقوله : { ليهلك من هلك } بدل من قوله : { ليقضي }

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r12.claim: At Badr the Muslims were few, poorly equipped, far from water on sinking sand; Meccans were numerous, armed, near water on firm ground, with the caravan and expected reinforcements. God reversed the outcome, a major miracle proving Muhammad’s promised victory.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r12.anchor: كانوا في غاية الخوف والضعف بسبب القلة وعدم الأهبة ، ونزلوا بعيدين عن الماء ، وكانت الأرض التي نزلوا فيها أرضا رملية

RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r13.claim: Those who perished did so after witnessing the miracle, and surviving believers witnessed it too; the ‘clear proof’ is this decisive miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v15p134/r13.anchor: والمؤمنون الذين بقوا في الحياة شاهدوا هذه المعجزة القاهرة ، والمراد من البينة هذه المعجزة

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r1.claim: One who has not been emptied of personal gain, desire, and attachment remains suspended between spiritual stations, still seeking benefit or reward.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r1.anchor: من لم يكن بك فانيا عن حظه . . . وعن الهوى والإنس والأحباب فكأنه - بين المراتب - واقف

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r2.claim: The battle of Badr and its circumstances unfolded by divine decree, not by human planning or deliberation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r2.anchor: يخبر - سبحانه - أن ما جرى يوم بدر من القتال ، وما حصل من فنون الأحوال كان بحكم التقدير ، لا بما يحصل من الخلق من التدبير

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r3.claim: Had the parties arranged the encounter, they would have recoiled from it and kept their distance; it occurred to fulfill the decree.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r3.anchor: بل لو كان ذلك على اختيار وتواعد ، كنتم عن تلك الجملة على استكراه وتباعد ، فجرى على ما جرى ليقضي الله أمرا

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r4.claim: The one who perishes is led astray after remaining behind a veil; the one who lives is guided after the proof has become clear.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r4.anchor: أي ليضل من زاغ عن الحق بعد لزومه الحجبة ، ويهتدي من أقام على الحق بعد وضوح الحجة

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r5.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r5.claim: Truth makes the path clear and establishes proof, yet God closes some people’s insight to guidance and opens others’ insight to the paths of truth.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r5.anchor: ويقال الحق أوضح السبيل ونصب الدليل ، ولكن سد بصائر قوم عن شهود الرشد ، وفتح بصائر آخرين لإدراك طرق الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r6.claim: The spiritually dead are those who fall into separation’s valleys; the spiritually alive live by the light of gnosis.

QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r7.claim: The spiritually dead remain bound to their own share, while the living are drawn away from every share.
QUSHAYRI:v1p396/r7.anchor: ويقال الهالك من كان بحظه مربوطا ، والحي من كان من أسر كل نصيب مستلبا مجذوبا

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r1.claim: At Badr the two armies stood on opposite sides of a valley, with Abū Sufyān's caravan below them toward the sea.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r1.anchor: the two armies were on two sides of a valley with the caravan of Abū Sufyān below them in the direction of the sea (R).

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r2.claim: Had they arranged to meet, the Muslims would not have agreed to face such a superior army had they known its strength.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r2.anchor: the Muslims would not have agreed to go out to meet such a superior army in battle if they had prior knowledge of it (Q)

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r3.claim: The matter God brought about was destined and necessarily had to come to pass.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r3.anchor: The battle is described as a matter that was to be done, meaning that it necessarily had to come to pass (R).

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r4.claim: The clear-proof wording echoes the separation of bad from good in 8:37 and the Badr Day of Discrimination, which exposed truth and falsehood through the battle.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r4.anchor: echoes the separation of the bad from the good in v. 37 and the idea that the Battle of Badr was a Day of Discrimination

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r5.claim: Some interpret the clear proof as the rain before battle, which reversed the Makkan advantage of firmer ground over the Muslims' soft ground.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r5.anchor: A clear proof is interpreted by some to refer to the rain that came just before the battle and miraculously reversed the advantage the Makkans had

STUDYQURAN:8:42/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r6.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r6.claim: Others understand the clear proof more broadly as the smaller, poorly equipped Muslim army's victory over Quraysh, three times its size and well armed.
STUDYQURAN:8:42/r6.anchor: others see it more broadly as the fact that the smaller and poorly equipped army of the Muslims defeated the well-armed contingent of Quraysh

SULAMI:v1p267#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r1.claim: God displayed signs, set up markers, opened some people's eyes and blinded others, and sent intermediaries with proofs and lights, yet guides to His light whom He wills; these precede destruction or life on clear proof.
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أظهر للخلق الآيات ، ونصب لهم الأعلام ، وفتح أعين قوم لرؤيتها

SULAMI:v1p267#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r2.claim: True life belongs only to one who lives through God's remembrance and nearness; all move through their causes, but the living person draws life from the Living who never dies.
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا حياة إلا لمن حيي بذكره وأنس بقربه ، والخلق كلهم متحركون في أسبابهم

SULAMI:v1p267#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r3.claim: What God decreed in eternity manifests over successive moments and times.
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r3.anchor: قال جعفر : ما قضاه الله في الأزل يظهره في الحين بعد الحين والوقت بعد الوقت

SULAMI:v1p267#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r4.claim: The event discloses God's prior knowledge in the unseen by bringing each faction to its pre-eternal allotment.
SULAMI:v1p267#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ليكشف عن سابق علمه في غيبه ، بإيصال كل من الفريقين إلى ما سبق له منه

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari frames the passage as assurance about the division of the Badr spoils for believers in God and the revelation to His servant, when God distinguished truth from falsehood by aiding His Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r1.anchor: واعلموا أن قسم الغنيمة على ما بينه لكم ربكم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله وما أنزل على عبده يوم بدر

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r2.claim: The Muslims stood by the valley edge nearer Medina, the polytheists at the far edge toward Mecca, and Abu Sufyan's caravan below them toward the seashore.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r2.anchor: يقول: بشفير الوادي الأدنى إلى المدينة {وهم بالعدوة القصوى} [الأنفال: 42] يقول: وعدوكم من المشركين نزول بشفير الوادي الأقصى إلى مكة

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the valley's edges were the opposing parties' locations, with the caravan below them belonging to Abu Sufyan and his companions.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا} [الأنفال: 42] قال: شفير الوادي الأدنى وهي بشفير الوادي الأقصى

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r4.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet was higher in the valley and the polytheists below him.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى} [الأنفال: 42] وهما شفيرا الوادي

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the caravan as the one the Muslims had set out to seize and Quraysh had set out to protect, with neither side arranging a meeting.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى} [الأنفال: 42] من الوادي إلى مكة

TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r6.claim: Mujahid recounts that Abu Sufyan's Syrian merchant caravan and the Muslims were unaware of one another until they met at Badr's water, fought, and the Muslims prevailed and took prisoners.
TAB-FULL:v11p203#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {والركب أسفل منكم} [الأنفال: 42] قال: أبو سفيان وأصحابه مقبلون من الشام تجارا، لم يشعروا بأصحاب بدر

TAB-FULL:v11p205/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r1.claim: Al-Suddi locates the two parties at opposite valley edges and identifies the caravan below the Muslims by the seashore as Abu Sufyan's.
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " ذكر منازل القوم والعير، فقال: {إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى} [الأنفال: 42] والركب: هو أبو سفيان وعيره، أسفل منكم على شاطئ البحر

TAB-FULL:v11p205/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r2.claim: Most Medinan and Kufan readers use ḍamma on the first vowel of al-ʿudwa; some Meccan and Basran readers use kasra. Both are established Arabic dialects with the same meaning, so either reading is correct.
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r2.anchor: فقرأ ذلك عامة قراء المدنيين والكوفيين: {بالعدوة} [الأنفال: 42] بضم العين

TAB-FULL:v11p205/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r3.speaker: الراعي
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r3.claim: Al-Rāʿī's cited verse uses العدوة with kasra and attests this form of the word.
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r3.anchor: ينشد بيت الراعي: [البحر المتقارب] وعينان حمر مآقيهما

TAB-FULL:v11p205/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r4.speaker: أوس بن حجر
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r4.claim: The cited line by Aws ibn Hajar supplies another poetic attestation for العدوة with kasra.
TAB-FULL:v11p205/r4.anchor: وكذلك ينشد بيت أوس بن حجر: [البحر البسيط] وفارس لو تحل الخيل عدوته

TAB-FULL:v11p206/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r1.claim: Had the two sides agreed to meet, the Muslims' smaller numbers would have made them miss the appointment; God instead gathered them unexpectedly to fulfill His decree by granting victory and killing or capturing the enemy at Badr.

TAB-FULL:v11p206/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the Muslims would have avoided a scheduled encounter after learning the enemy's numbers; God instead meant to exalt Islam and humble polytheism by His grace, not through the Muslims' prior planning.
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد} [الأنفال: 42] ولو كان ذلك عن ميعاد منكم ومنهم ثم بلغكم كثرة عددهم وقلة عددكم ما لقيتموهم

TAB-FULL:v11p206/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r3.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik reports that the Prophet and Muslims set out seeking Quraysh's caravan, and God brought them together with their enemy without an agreed appointment.
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r3.anchor: سمعت كعب بن مالك، يقول في غزوة بدر: «إنما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمون يريدون عير قريش، حتى جمع الله بينهم وبين عدوهم على غير ميعاد»

TAB-FULL:v11p206/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r4.speaker: عمير بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r4.claim: Umayr ibn Ishaq recounts that Abu Sufyan's Syrian caravan and Abu Jahl's force met at Badr without knowing of each other; the water carriers met first, then the fighters advanced.
TAB-FULL:v11p206/r4.anchor: عن عمير بن إسحاق، قال: " أقبل أبو سفيان في الركب من الشام، وخرج أبو جهل ليمنعه من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v11p208/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says the purpose lām in ليهلك is repeated from the lām in ليقضي, so the sense is that God gathered them so that whoever perished would perish upon clear proof.

TAB-FULL:v11p208/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r2.claim: God gathered them so that those who died did so after receiving established proof and witnessing a lesson, while those who lived did so with God's proof made clear to them.
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r2.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {ليهلك من هلك عن بينة} [الأنفال: 42] ليموت من مات من خلقه عن حجة لله قد أثبتت له، وقطعت عذره

TAB-FULL:v11p208/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses dying upon clear proof as seeing the signs and lessons, and living upon it as believing on that basis.
TAB-FULL:v11p208/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {ليهلك من هلك عن بينة،} [الأنفال: 42] لما رأى من الآيات والعبر

TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r1.claim: God hears believers and others when the Prophet is shown the enemy in a dream and each side sees the other as few, although numerous; He knows what people conceal in their hearts then and at all times.
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r1.anchor: فإن الله لا يخفى عليه خافية من ظاهر أو باطن

TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari exhorts all people to speak truthfully and keep sound beliefs in their hearts, since God knows everything outward and inward.
TAB-FULL:v11p208#2/r2.anchor: واتقوا ربكم أيها الناس في منطقكم أن تنطقوا بغير حق، وفي قلوبكم أن تعتقدوا فيها غير الرشد، فإن الله لا يخفى عليه خافية من ظاهر أو باطن

TAB-FULL:v11p212/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r1.claim: God made each side appear few to the other so they would fight, then gave the believers victory, raising God's word above the disbelievers' and fulfilling what He had decreed.

TAB-FULL:v11p212/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God brought them to battle to avenge those He chose and complete His favor upon those of His allegiance He chose to bless.
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا} [الأنفال: 42] أي ليؤلف بينهم على الحرب للنقمة ممن أراد الانتقام منه

TAB-FULL:v11p212/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r3.claim: Al-Tabari links the return of all affairs to God in the afterlife with His recompense of each person according to what they deserve.
TAB-FULL:v11p212/r3.anchor: مصير الأمور كلها إليه في الآخرة

TABATABAI:8:42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r1.claim: Al-ʿudwa is a valley’s edge (with ḍamma, sometimes kasra); dunyā is feminine of adnā, quṣwā (also quṣyā) feminine of aqṣā, and al-rakb is Abū Sufyān’s caravan.
TABATABAI:8:42/r1.anchor: العدوة بالضم وقد يكسر شفير الوادي، والدنيا مؤنث أدنى كما أن القصوى

TABATABAI:8:42/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r2.claim: The phrase ‘when you were at the nearer bank’ gives a second explanation of the preceding ‘day of the criterion’; ‘the day the two hosts met’ first explains the revelation upon the Prophet.
TABATABAI:8:42/r2.anchor: الظرف في قوله { إذ أنتم بالعدوة } بيان ثان لقوله في الآية السابقة { يوم الفرقان }

TABATABAI:8:42/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects attaching the time phrase to ‘God has power over everything’ as a strained reading meaning that God could aid them while they were weak near the valley.
TABATABAI:8:42/r3.anchor: وأما ما يظهر من بعضهم أنه بيان لقوله { والله على كل شيء قدير } بما يفيده بحسب المورد، والمعنى والله قدير

TABATABAI:8:42/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r4.claim: The armies did not plan to meet: Quraysh had numbers, water, and firm ground; the few Muslims had no water and unstable sand; Abū Sufyān’s caravan escaped down the coast, leaving both forces face to face with no escape.
TABATABAI:8:42/r4.anchor: لم يكن عن أسباب عادية بل لمشيئة خاصة إلهية ظهرت بها قدرته وبانت بها عنايته الخاصة

TABATABAI:8:42/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r5.claim: The meeting and Muslim victory resulted from special divine will, displaying God’s power, care, and support; ‘had you arranged a meeting’ signals that the encounter was not planned by either side.
TABATABAI:8:42/r5.anchor: فالتلاقي والمواجهة على هذا الوجه ثم ظهور المؤمنين على المشركين، لم يكن عن أسباب عادية

TABATABAI:8:42/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42/r6.claim: The purpose was to make truth and falsehood visibly clear, so that ‘perishing’ and ‘living’ mean misguidance and guidance, the outcomes connected to a manifest sign.
TABATABAI:8:42/r6.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن المراد بالهلاكة والحياة هو الهدى والضلال لأن ذلك هو الذي يرتبط به وجود الآية البينة ظاهرا

TABATABAI:8:42-44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r1.claim: ‘God is all-hearing, all-knowing’ coordinates with the purpose clause: God decreed the event because He heard their appeal and knew their hearts, recalling 8:9.
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله { ليهلك من هلك عن بينة } الخ، أي وإن الله إنما قضى ما قضى وفعل ما فعل لأنه سميع يسمع دعاءكم

TABATABAI:8:42-44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r2.claim: The dream, Satan’s beautification of deeds, and the hypocrites’ claim that faith deluded the believers continue the account to show that this event came from special divine decree rather than ordinary causes.
TABATABAI:8:42-44/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا السياق - أي لبيان أن مرجع الأمر في هذه الواقعة هو القضاء الخاص الإلهي دون الأسباب العادية - سيق قوله تعالى بعد

AKHFASH:v1p350/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p350/r1.claim: Although all God's commands come to pass, this phrasing states the argument against them and removes their excuse before their destruction.
AKHFASH:v1p350/r1.anchor: وامر الله كله مفعول ولكن اراد أن يقص الاحتجاج عليهم وقطع العذر قبل اهلاكهم

AKHFASH:v1p350/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p350/r2.claim: Both عدوة and عدوة are language forms; the author reads the former, while some use the latter.
AKHFASH:v1p350/r2.anchor: وقال {إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا} وقال بعضهم {بالعدوة} وبها نقرأ وهما لغتان

AKHFASH:v1p350/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p350/r3.claim: Some eloquent Arabs say العدية, replacing wāw with yāʾ, as in شروى and بلوى and other related forms.

AKHFASH:v1p350/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p350/r4.claim: أسفل is used adverbially as a locative; it can also be predicated of الركب instead of treated as an adverb.

AKHFASH:v1p350/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p350/r5.claim: The author requires assimilation in يحيى here because the form is in a position requiring fatḥa, like a doubled verb.
AKHFASH:v1p350/r5.anchor: فالزم الادغام اذ صار في موضع يلزمه الفتح فصار مثل باب التضعيف

AKHFASH:v1p350/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r7.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p350/r7.claim: Some read حيي without assimilation; the author calls this the worse form because حيي behaves like خشي, and cites poetry with حيوا.
AKHFASH:v1p350/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم {من حيي عن بينة} ولم يدغم اذا كان لا يدغمه في سائر ذلك. وهذا أقبح الوجهين

AKHFASH:v1p350/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p350/r8.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p350/r8.claim: Some retain the doubled form with heaviness and no assimilation; the author calls this ugly and cites a poem with عيوا.
AKHFASH:v1p350/r8.anchor: وقد ثقل بعضهم وتركها على ما كانت عليه وذلك قبيح. قال الشاعر:

TABRISI:8:42/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
TABRISI:8:42/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read al-ʿidwa with kasra; the other readers use ḍamma.
TABRISI:8:42/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالعدوة بكسر العين والباقون بضمها

TABRISI:8:42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r2.speaker: الراعي
TABRISI:8:42/r2.claim: The Rāʿī's verse witnesses the kasra form of al-ʿidwa.
TABRISI:8:42/r2.anchor:
قال الراعي: في الكسر:
وعينان حم مآقيهما

TABRISI:8:42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r3.speaker: أوس بن حجر
TABRISI:8:42/r3.claim: Aws ibn Ḥajar's verse witnesses the ḍamma form of al-ʿidwa.
TABRISI:8:42/r3.anchor: وقال أوس بن حجر في الضم: وفارس لا يحل الحي عدوته

TABRISI:8:42/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r4.speaker: نافع، أبو بكر عن عاصم، البزي عن ابن كثير
TABRISI:8:42/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr pronounce both yāʾs in ḥayiya; the others assimilate them.
TABRISI:8:42/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم والبزي عن ابن كثير حيي بإظهار اليائين والباقون حي بالإدغام

TABRISI:8:42/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r5.claim: Assimilation is explained by movement on the second yāʾ; pronouncing both yāʾs preserves the pattern of the present yaḥyā.
TABRISI:8:42/r5.anchor: ومن أدغم حي فللزوم الحركة في الثاني فجرى مجرى ردوا

TABRISI:8:42/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r6.claim: Al-ʿidwa is the bank or edge of a valley; a valley has two banks, and its plural forms are ʿudan and ʿudiyy.
TABRISI:8:42/r6.anchor: العدوة شفير الوادي وللوادي عدوتان وهما جانباه والجمع عدى وعدي

TABRISI:8:42/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r7.claim: Al-dunyā is the feminine of al-adnā and al-quṣwā the feminine of al-aqṣā; wāw-root fuʿlā adjectives usually shift to yāʾ, though Hijazis rarely retain wāw in al-quṣwā.
TABRISI:8:42/r7.anchor: والدنيا تأنيث الأدنى من دنوت والقصوى تأنيث الأقصى وما كان من النعوت على فعلى من بنات الواو

TABRISI:8:42/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r8.claim: Al-aqṣā means farther, al-qaṣā means distance, and qaṣawtu means I moved away; non-Hijazis say al-qaṣyā.
TABRISI:8:42/r8.anchor: إلا أن أهل الحجاز قالوا القصوى فأظهروا الواو وهو نادر وغيرهم يقولون القصيا والأقصى الأبعد

TABRISI:8:42/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r9.claim: Rكب is a collective plural for rider, like shārib/sharb and ṣāḥib/ṣaḥb.
TABRISI:8:42/r9.anchor: والركب جمع راكب مثل شارب وشرب وصاحب وصحب

TABRISI:8:42/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r10.claim: The upper is a level with a level beneath it, and the lower a level with a level above it.
TABRISI:8:42/r10.anchor: والعلو قرار تحته قرار والسفل قرار فوقه قرار

TABRISI:8:42/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r18.claim: Asfal is accusative either because an omitted phrase means at a lower place or as a locative adverb; it may also be raised to mean more below.
TABRISI:8:42/r18.anchor: إنما نصب أسفل لأن تقديره بمكان أسفل أو في مكان أسفل

TABRISI:8:42/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:8:42/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Muslims camped at the nearer bank, nearer Medina, while God could grant victory despite their weakness.
TABRISI:8:42/r19.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد والله قدير على نصركم وأنتم أذلة

TABRISI:8:42/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r20.claim: The far bank was occupied by the polytheists, the opposing army that had come out to battle.

TABRISI:8:42/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r21.claim: The caravan was Abū Sufyān and his companions, below the Muslims by the sea; al-Kalbī places it three miles away on the shore.
TABRISI:8:42/r21.anchor: يعني أبا سفيان وأصحابه وهم العير

TABRISI:8:42/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42/r22.claim: Muslims lacked water, numbers, and equipment, and their feet sank in sand, while the enemy had more men, supplies, and water; victory nevertheless came from God.
TABRISI:8:42/r22.anchor: وما كان المسلمون فيه من قلة الماء والرمل الذي تسوخ فيه الأرجل مع قلة العدد والعدة

TABRISI:8:42-43/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TABRISI:8:42-43/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says that hearing the enemy's numbers while knowing their own weakness would have made the Muslims retreat and break the appointment.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r1.anchor: معناه لو تواعدتم أيها المسلمون للاجتماع في الموضع الذي اجتمعتم فيه

TABRISI:8:42-43/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:42-43/r2.claim: Another explanation is that obstacles would have caused them to miss the time; mentioning the appointment emphasizes their agreement and God's kindness.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه لاختلفتم بما يعرض من العوائق والقواطع فذكر الميعاد لتأكيد أمره

TABRISI:8:42-43/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r3.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:8:42-43/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's line says the winds crossed their homes as if the people had been expected, illustrating an apparently appointed meeting.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r3.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: جرت الرياح على محل ديارهم فكأنهم كانوا على ميعاد

TABRISI:8:42-43/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42-43/r4.claim: God brought the armies together without planning so His inevitable decree would manifest, strengthening Islam and humiliating polytheism.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r4.anchor: معناه ولكن قدر الله تعالى التقاءكم وجمع بينكم وبينهم على غير ميعاد منكم

TABRISI:8:42-43/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42-43/r5.claim: Here li-yaqḍiya means to manifest the decree, since God has already decreed what will occur.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r5.anchor: ومعنى ليقضي ليظهر قضاءه إذ الله تعالى قد قضى ما هو كائن

TABRISI:8:42-43/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42-43/r6.claim: Mafʿūlan means certain to occur, an inevitable matter already settled.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r6.anchor: يقال للأمر الكائن لا محالة هذا أمر مفروغ منه

TABRISI:8:42-43/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:42-43/r7.claim: Another explanation is that God fulfilled a matter already in His knowledge: making Islam manifest and exalting it over idol worshippers.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه ليتم أمرا كان في علمه مفعولا لا محالة

TABRISI:8:42-43/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42-43/r8.claim: People died or lived only after the Prophet's evident miracles, including in battle, established proof for them.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r8.anchor: أي فعل ذلك ليموت من مات منهم بعد قيام الحجة عليه بما رأى من المعجزات

TABRISI:8:42-43/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:42-43/r9.claim: One view says the proof was God's promise of victory to believers, confirming the Prophet's truthfulness.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن البينة هي وعد الله من النصر للمؤمنين على الكافرين

TABRISI:8:42-43/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:42-43/r10.claim: Another view treats an unbeliever's continued life after proof as ruin and a believer's continued faith as life; ʿan bayyina means after clarification.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه ليهلك من ضل بعد قيام الحجة عليه فتكون حياة الكافر

TABRISI:8:42-43/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:42-43/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:42-43/r11.claim: God hears words, knows inner thoughts, and recompenses people according to what they do.
TABRISI:8:42-43/r11.anchor: فهو يجازيهم بحسب ما يكون منهم

FARRA:v1p410/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p410/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p410/r9.claim: The nearer bank is the side of the valley toward Medina; the farther bank faces Mecca.
FARRA:v1p410/r9.anchor: والعدوة: شاطئ الوادي الدنيا مما يلي المدينة، والقصوى مما يلي مكة.

FARRA:v1p410/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p410/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p410/r10.claim: The caravan was Abū Sufyān’s, on the seashore.
FARRA:v1p410/r10.anchor: يعني أبا سفيان والعير، كانوا على شاطئ البحر.

FARRA:v1p410/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p410/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p410/r11.claim: أسفل is accusative as an implied place, مكانا أسفل منكم; describing them as lower with أشد تسفلا would permit nominative.
FARRA:v1p410/r11.anchor: نصبت يريد: مكانا أسفل منكم. ولو وصفهم بالتسفل وأراد: والركب أشد تسفلا لجاز ورفع.

FARRA:v1p410/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p410/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p410/r12.claim: Most readers assimilate the two yāʾs in حيّ; some pronounce both. Assimilation works with the dual, but the excerpt cuts off as it begins to explain the plural.
FARRA:v1p410/r12.anchor: ويحيى من حي عن بينة كتابتها على الادغام بياء واحدة، وهي أكثر قراءة القراء.

THALABI:v4p361/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r5.claim: The nearer bank was toward Medina and the farther bank away from Medina; the caravan was below the Muslims toward the seacoast, while the Prophet and polytheists occupied opposite parts of the valley.
THALABI:v4p361/r5.anchor: يا معشر المسلمين بالعدوة الدنيا شفير الوادي الأدنى إلى المدينة وهم يعني عدوكم من المشركين بالعدوة القصوى من الوادي الأقصى من المدينة

THALABI:v4p361/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r6.claim: Readers differ between kasra and ḍamma on the ʿayn; Meccan and Basran readers use kasra, while the rest use ḍamma, both established dialect forms.
THALABI:v4p361/r6.anchor: وفي العدوة قراءتان: كسر العين وهو قراءة أهل مكة والبصرة. وضم العين وهو قرأ الباقين واختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

THALABI:v4p361/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r7.claim: Poetry by al-Raʿi witnesses the kasra form, while a line by Aws ibn Hajar witnesses the ḍamma form.
THALABI:v4p361/r7.anchor: وينشد بيت الراعي: وعينان حمر مآقيهما

THALABI:v4p361/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r8.claim: Dunyā is the feminine form of adnā, and quṣwā the feminine form of aqṣā.
THALABI:v4p361/r8.anchor: والدنيا تأنيث الأدنى، والقصوى تأنيث الأقصى

THALABI:v4p361/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r9.claim: The Muslims had set out to intercept the caravan and the unbelievers to protect it, so they unexpectedly met; an agreed meeting would have failed because of the Muslims' small numbers and the enemy's size.
THALABI:v4p361/r9.anchor: وكان المسلمون خرجوا ليأخذوا العير وخرج الكفار ليمنعوها فالتقوا من غير ميعاد قال الله ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد لقلتكم وكثرة عدوكم

THALABI:v4p361/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r10.claim: God brought about His ordained matter by helping His allies, exalting His religion, and destroying His enemies; the lām in ليهلك repeats the purpose lām in ليقضي.
THALABI:v4p361/r10.anchor: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا من نصر أوليائه وإعزاز دينه وإهلاك أعدائه ليهلك هذه اللام مكررة على اللام

THALABI:v4p361/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p361/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p361/r11.claim: To perish or live on clear proof means to face evidence witnessed and established against one; the author links this to the rule that God does not punish before sending a messenger.
THALABI:v4p361/r11.anchor: عن بينة أي ليموت من يموت على بينة [ولها وعبرة] عاينها

THALABI:v4p362/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p362/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
THALABI:v4p362/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the unbeliever rejects after a proof has removed his excuse, while the believer believes upon proof.
THALABI:v4p362/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: ليكفر من كفر بعد حجة قامت عليه وقطعت معذرته ويؤمن من آمن

THALABI:v4p362/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p362/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p362/r2.claim: Qatada says whoever strays does so on clear proof, and whoever is guided is guided on clear proof.
THALABI:v4p362/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: ليضل من ضل عن بينة ويهتدي من اهتدى على بينة

THALABI:v4p362/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p362/r3.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v4p362/r3.claim: Ata explains perishing as knowing the wrongdoing one enters and living as knowing and being certain of there is no god but God.
THALABI:v4p362/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: ليهلك من هلك عن بينة عن علم بما دخل فيه من الفجور ويحيى من حي عن بينة عن علم ويقين

THALABI:v4p362/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p362/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p362/r4.claim: Medinan readers read حيي with two yās, while the rest read حي with one doubled yā by assimilation, matching the written form.
THALABI:v4p362/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة: (حيي) بيائين مثل خشيي على الإيمان

THALABI:v4p363/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p363/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p363/r3.claim: The ordained event was already in God's knowledge: Islam and its people would prevail, while unbelief and its people would be humbled.
THALABI:v4p363/r3.anchor: ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا كائنا في علمه، نصير الإسلام وأهله ذل الشرك وأهله

THALABI:v4p363/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p363/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
THALABI:v4p363/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the decree meant vengeance on God's enemies and favor to His allies.
THALABI:v4p363/r4.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا بالانتقام من أعدائه والإنعام على أوليائه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r1.claim: إذ may depend on an omitted imperative, remember when you were there, as at 8:26; alternatively it may depend on الفرقان in يوم الفرقان.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تتعلق (إذ) بمضمر معناه: واذكروا إذ أنتم، كما قال تعالى: {واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل} [الأنفال: 26]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r2.claim: Alternatively, إذ may depend on الفرقان in يوم الفرقان, referring to God's distinction between truth and falsehood there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تتعلق بالمصدر الذي هو (الفرقان) في قوله: {يوم الفرقان} المعنى: يوم فرق الله بين الحق والباطل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit defines ʿudwah as a valley's side and gives its plural forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: عدوة الوادي وعدوته: جانبه والجمع عدى وعدى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r4.claim: Al-Layth defines ʿudwah as firm ground at a valley's bank and notes another pronunciation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r4.anchor: وقال الليث: العدوة: صلابة من شاطئ الوادي ويقال: عدوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r5.claim: Both linguistic forms of ʿudwah are read.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r6.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash says the kasra form is the only one heard from Arabs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش: الكسر كلام العرب، لم يسمع منهم غير ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r7.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r7.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says the damma form is the more common of the two dialects.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r7.anchor: قال أحمد بن يحيى: الضم في العدوة أكثر اللغتين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r8.claim: Dunyā is the feminine of adnā and quṣwā the feminine of aqṣā; قصا means to be distant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r8.anchor: و {الدنيا}: تأنيث الأدنى، وضده القصوى، وهو تأنيث الأقصى، وكل شيء تنحى عن شيء فقد قصى يقصو (¬1) قصوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r9.speaker: ابن السكيت عن الحراني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit, through al-Harrani, says adjectives such as الدنيا take yāʾ because wāw after initial ḍamma is heavy; Hijaz preserves القصوى while Tamim says القصيا.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r9.anchor: قال الحراني عن ابن السكيت: ما كان من النعوت مثل العليا والدنيا فإنه يأتي بضم أوله وبالياء؛ لأنهم يستثقلون الواو مع ضمة أوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r10.speaker: الخليل عن الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r10.claim: Al-Khalil, as transmitted by al-Layth, says fُعلى forms from wāw roots usually shift to yāʾ, as دنيا from دنوت; القصوى is exceptional, while القصيا and Medinan فتوى also occur.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r10.anchor: ونحو هذا حكى الليث عن الخليل فقال: كل شيء جاء على (فعلى) من بنات (¬4) الواو فإن العرب تحوله إلى الياء نحو: الدنيا من دنوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r11.speaker: المفسرون جميعا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r11.claim: All exegetes say the Muslims stood at the valley's near edge toward Medina and their enemy at the far edge toward Mecca; the forces camped on opposite banks at Badr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r11.anchor: قال المفسرون جميعا: إذ أنتم نزول بشفير (¬1) الوادي الأدنى إلى المدينة وعدوكم نزول بشفير الوادي الأقصى إلى مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r12.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r12.claim: The اهل المعاني say this recalls the nearer bank by Medina and farther bank opposite it; God's subtle arrangement kept Muslims closer to home and steadier in courage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p166/r12.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: معنى (¬3) الآية: اذكروا إذ كنتم بشط الوادي الأقرب (¬4) إلى المدينة وهم بالشط الأبعد منها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r1.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r1.claim: Al-Rakb means camel riders, numbering ten or more.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r1.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: الركب أصحاب الإبل، وهم العشرة فما فوقها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r2.claim: The caravan below the Muslims was Abu Sufyan and his companions, positioned toward the sea coast.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: يعني أبا سفيان وأصحابه وهم العير التي خرجوا ليأخذوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r3.claim: Safala means to be below, the opposite of rising above.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r3.anchor: ويقال: سفل يسفل سفاله وسفلا فهو سافل، نقيض علا يعلو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Farrāʾ favor accusative as read, with an implied “place”; nominative is also possible meaning “more below.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: الوجه أن تنصب (أسفل) -وعليه القراءة- أراد: مكانا أسفل، ويجوز الرفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r5.claim: Abū Sufyan's Syrian caravan, the Prophet and his companions seeking it, and Quraysh trying to protect it met at Badr without knowing they would meet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r5.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: أقبل أبو سفيان في الركب من الشام، وخرج رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r6.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r6.claim: Given the Muslims' small numbers and Quraysh's large force, learning the disparity after an appointment would have made the Muslims delay and break it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r6.anchor: لكثرتهم وقلتكم، يعني: لو تواعدتم ثم بلغكم كثرة عددهم مع قلة عددكم لتأخرتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r7.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r7.claim: Another explanation is that without God's favor, obstacles and impediments would have caused the parties to miss the appointment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p168/r7.anchor: وقيل: لو تواعدتم من غير لطف الله لكم لاختلفتم بالعوائق والقواطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r1.claim: The clause omits “God gathered you without an appointment”; it may be supplied before the purpose clause or after it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r1.anchor: في الكلام حذف واختصار يدل عليه الفحوى، تقديره: ولكن جمعكم الله من غير ميعاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r2.claim: God completed His promised appointment for His Prophet and the believers, bringing joy to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r2.anchor: قال ابن # عباس: يريد: ليتم الله لنبيه وللمؤمنين موعده؛ ليقر عين نبيه وأعين المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r3.claim: God brought to pass what was already in His knowledge and judgment: Islam's triumph over idol worship through His providence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: ليفصل (¬2) الله أمرا كان مفعولا في علمه وحكمه من عز الإسلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r4.claim: The purpose lām in “so that he perishes” repeats the lām in “so that He may decree”; the sense is that God acted for this purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r4.anchor: فهذه اللام مكررة على اللام في قوله: {ليقضي} المعنى: ولكن فعل ذلك ليهلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r5.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r5.claim: Most scholars understand perishing as disbelief and misguidance, and life as guidance and Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r5.anchor: وأكثر أهل العلم على أن المراد بالهلاك هاهنا: الكفر والضلال، وبالحياة: الاهتداء والإسلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r6.claim: Disbelief follows an established proof that leaves no excuse, and belief likewise follows such proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: ليكفر من كفر بعد حجة قامت عليه وقطعت عذره، ويؤمن من آمن على مثل ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r7.claim: Those who go astray do so on clear evidence, and those guided are guided on clear evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: ليضل من ضل عن بينة، ويهتدي (¬6) من اهتدى على بينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the wording metaphorically: those oriented toward truth are treated as living, while the misguided are treated as perished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: جعل الله عز وجل المقاصد للحق بمنزلة الحي، وجعل الضال بمنزلة الهالك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r9.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r9.claim: Another view takes perishing and living literally as death and life: at Badr, each would die or survive after seeing proof, in keeping with the promise to send a messenger before punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p169/r9.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن معنى الهلاك هاهنا: الموت (¬1)، وقال (¬2): وأفعل ما فعلت يوم بدر ليكون موت من يموت على بينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r1.claim: The verb is read with two yāʾs or with one geminated yāʾ; Abū Isḥāq explains the latter by assimilation and the former by the second radical's derivation from yāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أما من أدغم فلاجتماع حرفين من جنس واحد، وأما من أظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says assimilation is possible when the final yāʾ has a fixed vowel and therefore behaves like a sound consonant; he cites forms and Qurʾanic examples.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r2.anchor: من أدغم فلأن الياء قد لزمتها الحركة، فصار (¬6) بلزوم الحركة له مشابها للصحيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r3.speaker: المتلمس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r3.claim: Al-Mutalammis's poetic line uses “ḥayyu” with assimilation, illustrating the grammatical case for assimilating a yāʾ whose vowel is fixed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r3.anchor: وقال المتلبس (¬2): فهذا أوان العرض حي ذبابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r4.claim: Assimilation requires the affected yāʾ's vowel to be fixed; it is disallowed in “to give life to the dead” because the accusative vowel can change in other inflections.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r4.anchor: عبرة هذا: أن [كل موضع لزمت الحركة الياء الأخيرة التي هي لام جاز الإدغام فيه]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that showing both yāʾs is preferable when the final vowel can disappear in inflection; Yunus's forms أحيياء and أحييه show separation even with a stable vowel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p171/r5.anchor: وأما من أظهر فقال: (حيي) ولم يدغم فلأن حركة اللام في (حيي) تزول لاتصالها بالضمير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p174/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p174/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p174/r1.claim: God hears the believers' prayers, supplication, and pleading, and knows their intentions, love for Him, support for His Prophet, and obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p174/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: سميع لدعائكم وابتهالكم وتضرعكم، عليم بنياتكم وحبكم لربكم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#3/r1.claim: Al-ʿudwa is the edge or bank of a valley; the word is also pronounced with a different vowel.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#3/r1.anchor: العدوة} شفير الوادي. يقال: عدوة الوادي وعدوته.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r1.claim: The Muslims camped on the valley's near edge toward Medina; their enemies were on its far edge toward Mecca.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r1.anchor: { إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا } نزول بشفير الوادي الأدنى إلى المدينة، وعدوكم نزول بشفير الوادي الأقصى إلى مكة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r2.claim: The caravan was Abu Sufyan and his camel-owning companions, down by the seacoast.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r2.anchor: { والركب } أبو سفيان وأصحابه، وهم أصحاب الإبل. يعني: العير { أسفل منكم } إلى ساحل البحر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r3.claim: Had they arranged the battle, they would have delayed and broken the agreement because the enemy was many and they few.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r3.anchor: { ولو تواعدتم } للقتال { لاختلفتم في الميعاد } لتأخرتم فنقضتم الميعاد لكثرتهم وقلتكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r4.claim: God gathered them without an appointment to fulfill His foreknown purpose: victory for the Prophet and believers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r4.anchor: { ولكن } جمعكم الله من غير ميعاد { ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا } في علمه وحكمه من نصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r5.claim: Disbelief and belief followed clear proof; the proof was the believers' victory despite fewer numbers against a larger, stronger force.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r5.anchor: { ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة } أي: فعل ذلك ليضل ويكفر من كفر من بعد حجة قامت عليه، وقطعت عذره، ويؤمن من آمن على مثل ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r6.claim: God hears their prayers and knows their intentions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:42-44/r6.anchor: { وإن الله لسميع } لدعائكم { عليم } بنياتكم.

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r3.claim: The believers were on the near bank in a poor position, while the enemy held the more favorable far bank; the caravan was below them by the shore.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r3.anchor: siz vâdinin beri kıyısında -fena bir mevki‘de- idiniz

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r4.claim: The caravan was below and under the Muslims' threat, but its presence could embolden the enemy and unsettle the Muslims; overall military conditions favored the enemy.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r4.anchor: bunlar düşman ordusunun sizi işgal edecek ve aynı zamanda harbe hırslarını tahrik edecek bir kuvveti ve bu vaziyet sizi korkutacak

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r5.claim: Had the armies agreed on a meeting after recognizing the imbalance, the Muslims would have lost courage, broken the appointment, and avoided the fight; human planning alone could not have produced this victory.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r5.anchor: bu vaziyete gelince cesaret edemez, vaadinizde hulf eder, zaferden me’yus olurdunuz.

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r6.claim: Without a prior appointment and without leaving them to themselves, God brought the two sides together to enact His decree, distinguish truth from falsehood and allies from enemies, and establish His promised aid as decisive proof.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r6.anchor: Allah o fiile çıkan emri o hârikulâde emr-i vâki‘i; o vaziyeti

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r7.claim: Badr was a visible sign and proof: those who opposed God and His Messenger perished or would perish, while obedient believers gained or would gain material or spiritual life and salvation.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r7.anchor: Allah’ın öyle bir âyet-i vâzıhası ve öyle bir beyyine-i meşhûdesidir ki

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r8.claim: After this manifest proof, neither the dead nor living, unbeliever nor believer, can present an argument or excuse against God.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r8.anchor: ne ölünün ne dirinin, ne kâfirin ne mü’minin Allah’a karşı ne ibraz edebilecek bir hücceti ne de serd edebilecek bir mazereti yoktur

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r9.claim: God hears what His friends and enemies say, knows their intentions, beliefs, aims, and secrets, and knows what He will do concerning them.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r9.anchor: Dostlarının düşmanlarının söylediklerini işitir, niyet ve itikadlarını, maksat ve muzmerlerini ve haklarında ne yapacağını bilir.

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r10.claim: This closing phrase reinforces the ending of 8:17 and directs attention back to it.

ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r11.claim: Extraordinary events and miracles are not products of chance.
ELMALILI:8:41-43#2/r11.anchor: Hâsılı havârik ve mu‘cizât bir eser-i tesadüf değildir.

MAJAZ:v1p246/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p246/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p246/r1.claim: Al-ʿidwa is read with kasra, though some use ḍamma; it means the edge or bank of a valley, either side, like a well’s rim.
MAJAZ:v1p246/r1.anchor: بالعدوة الدنيا» (42) مكسورة، وبعضهم يضمها، ومجازه من: عدى الوادي أي ملطاط شفيره

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r1.claim: When Abu Sufyan learned the Muslims were heading to intercept the caravan, he left the Mecca road through Badr and took the lower coastal route.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r1.anchor: Ebû Süfyân, müslümanların kervanı vurmak üzere yola çıktıklarını haber alınca Bedir’den geçerek Mekke’ye ulaşan yolu terketmiş, râkımı daha düşük olan sahil yoluna kaymıştı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r2.claim: The Muslim position was dangerous because enemy caravan guards lay on the sea side and Abu Jahl's army faced them, leaving the Muslims between two forces.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r2.anchor: Deniz tarafında korumalarıyla birlikte düşman kervanı, karşı tarafta ise Ebû Cehil kumandasındaki düşman askerleri vardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r3.claim: The Meccans had the more suitable firm ground farther from Medina, while the Muslims were forced onto sand that impeded movement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r3.anchor: Mekkeliler’in daha önce gelerek mevzilendikleri, Medine’ye daha uzak bulunan yer hareket için daha uygun, kumsuz ve sağlam zeminli bir mekân olduğu halde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r4.claim: Rain was an extraordinary divine aid: it firmed the Muslims' sand and increased their water, while turning the enemy's position muddy and hindering movement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r4.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın bu savaşta müslümanlara olağan üstü yardımları cümlesinden olarak kumu pekiştiren, ihtiyaç duyulan suyu çoğaltan yağmur yağdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r5.claim: Another divine favor was that the enemy failed to realize the Muslims were between their forces and did not attempt a pincer maneuver.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r5.anchor: düşmanlar, müslümanları araya aldıklarının farkında olamadılar ve bir kıskaç harekâtına teşebbüs edemediler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r6.claim: Prior calculations about when and where the armies would arrive failed; events unfolded better than expected because God willed Muslim victory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r6.anchor: Mevzilere geliş zamanı ve yerleşmeleri konusunda önceden yapılabilecek hesaplar tutmamış, olanlar düşünülebileceklerden daha hayırlı olarak tecelli etmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r7.claim: Had the sides tried to negotiate the timing and positions, disagreement would have resulted and their decision might have reduced the Muslims' chance of victory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r7.anchor: Bunlara kendi aralarında veya karşı taraf ile müzakere yoluyla karar vermeye kalkışsalardı elbette her kafadan bir ses çıkacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r8.claim: God's help was unmistakable evidence of who was on the right path and acting in accord with His approval, and who opposed it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r8.anchor: Bu savaşta Allah’ın yardımı ve desteği çok açıktı, bu açıklık kimin doğru yolda olduğuna, Allah’ın rızâsına uygun davrandığına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r9.claim: After such clear proof there was no excuse for persisting in error; those fighting or dying for truth or falsehood knew, or should have known, what their cause meant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:42/r9.anchor: Bunca açık delili gördükten sonra hâlâ gafletten uyanmayan, yanlış yoldan dönmeyen kimseler için mazeret kalmamıştı

BURHAN:v3p64/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p64/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p64/r1.claim: احتراس adds a phrase when speech could bear a distant interpretation, closing off that unwanted possibility.
BURHAN:v3p64/r1.anchor: وهو أن يكون الكلام محتملا لشيء بعيد فيؤتى بما يدفع ذلك الاحتمال

NAHHAS:v2p188/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r1.claim: The plural of عدوة is عدى; the same plural is used by those who pronounce the singular عدوة, as in لحية and لحى.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r1.anchor: والجمع عدى ومن قال عدوة قال عدى مثل لحية ولحى

NAHHAS:v2p188/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r2.claim: القصيا is also said for القصوى; its original consonant is wāw.

NAHHAS:v2p188/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r3.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p188/r3.claim: One view identifies the caravan as the camels carrying the opponents' goods, placed safely by God's providence as a reminder of His favor.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r3.anchor: قيل يعني به الإبل التي كانت تحمل أمتعتهم وكانت في موضع يأمنون عليها توفيقا من الله

NAHHAS:v2p188/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r4.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p188/r4.claim: Another view takes الركب to mean the Quraysh caravan.

NAHHAS:v2p188/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r5.claim: أسفل منكم can be an adverbial phrase functioning as the predicate: the caravan was in a place lower than you.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r5.anchor: أسفل منكم ) ظرف في موضع الخبر أي موضعا أسفل منكم

NAHHAS:v2p188/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r6.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v2p188/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī, and al-Farrāʾ allow أسفل to mean more steeply or farther below you.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r6.anchor: وأجاز الأخفش والكسائي والفراء والركب أسفل منكم أي أشد تسفلا منكم

NAHHAS:v2p188/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r7.claim: الركب is a collective plural of راكب used for a group mounted on camels; Ibn al-Sikkīt and most linguists reserve راكب and ركب for camel riders, not riders of horses or other mounts.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r7.anchor: والركب جمع راكب ولا تقول العرب ركب إلا للجماعة الراكبي الإبل وحكى ابن السكيت وأكثر أهل اللغة

NAHHAS:v2p188/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r8.claim: Had the parties arranged a meeting, they would not have agreed on its timing; God instead brought them together there.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r8.anchor: ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد ) أي لم يكن يقع الاتفاق فوفق الله جل وعز لكم

NAHHAS:v2p188/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r9.claim: The purpose was for God to accomplish the destined matter of granting victory to the believers.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r9.anchor: ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ) من نصر المؤمنين

NAHHAS:v2p188/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r10.claim: The lām in ليهلك is purposive and repeats the lām in ليقضي; من is nominative, while ويحيا is accusative.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r10.anchor: ليهلك من هلك ) لام كي والتقدير ولكن جمعكم هنالك ليقضي أمرا ليهلك هذه اللام مكررة

NAHHAS:v2p188/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير وحمزة
NAHHAS:v2p188/r11.claim: These readers assimilate the two yāʾs in حيّ, a reading preferred by Sībawayh and Abū ʿUbayd.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r11.anchor: هذه قراءة أبي عمرو وابن كثير وحمزة وهي اختيار سيبويه وأبي عبيد

NAHHAS:v2p188/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r12.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v2p188/r12.claim: Abū ʿUbayd supports assimilation because the written consonantal text has one yāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar says this omission in the script is not decisive.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r12.anchor: فأما احتجاج أبي عبيد فإنه في السواد بياء واحدة قال أبو جعفر هذا الاحتجاج لا يلزم

NAHHAS:v2p188/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r13.claim: The expert grammarians favor assimilation when two identical consonants meet in pronunciation, as in جف.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r13.anchor: اجتماع النحويين الحذاق في هذا أنه لما اجتمع حرفان على لفظ واحد كان الأولى الإدغام كما يقال جف

NAHHAS:v2p188/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r14.speaker: نافع وعاصم
NAHHAS:v2p188/r14.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read حيى without assimilation, analogizing the present to the past because they disallow assimilation in the present.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r14.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم ( من حيى عن بينة ) والحجة لهما أنه لا يجوز الإدغام في المستقبل

NAHHAS:v2p188/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r15.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p188/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits assimilation in the present, including يحيى; Abū Jaʿfar rejects this as a major grammatical error.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r15.anchor: وقد أجاز الفراء الإدغام في المستقبل وأن يدغم يحيى وهذا عند جميع البصريين من الخطأ الكبير

NAHHAS:v2p188/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p188/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p188/r16.claim: Assimilation is impossible here because the second yāʾ in يحيى is quiescent, unlike cases such as لم يجف; it is also forbidden in أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيى الموتى because the vowel is accidental.
NAHHAS:v2p188/r16.anchor: العلة في منعه أنك إذا قلت يحيى فالياء الثانية ساكنة فلم يجتمع حرفان متحركان فيدغم

BURHAN:v1p481/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p481/r4.speaker: علي
BURHAN:v1p481/r4.claim: ʿAli included the Qur'anic phrase that God might bring about a matter already decreed while saying he was pledging allegiance to their companion.

ITQAN:v2p341/r29.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p341/r29.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p341/r29.claim: The nearer side of the valley is its bank.

ITQAN:v2p414/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p414/r23.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p414/r23.claim: Qaḍā can mean carrying out or bringing to pass a matter already decreed.
ITQAN:v2p414/r23.anchor: 5 والمضي ﴿ ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ﴾
